model.ccp.core_appeals_lifecycle_legacy.name: core_appeals_lifecycle_legacy
model.ccp.core_appeals_lifecycle_legacy.raw_code:
-- Core Appeals Lifecycle entity (LEGACY system, TrafficGuard/NewLogic).
-- Grain = 1 row per appeal_id from core_appeal_legacy.
--
-- This model enriches the base legacy appeal entity with:
--   - appeal lifecycle stages
--   - POPLA lifecycle information
--   - final appeal outcome
--   - discount-applied flag
--
-- The model is shaped to align with core_appeals_lifecycle for the live
-- Zeus/Dataverse estate.

{{ config(
    materialized = 'table',
    alias = 'core_appeals_lifecycle_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'legacy', 'appeals_lifecycle']
) }}

WITH popla_code_flag AS (

    SELECT DISTINCT
        TRIM(UPPER(pcn)) AS pcn_id
    FROM {{ ref('popla_code') }}
    WHERE pcn IS NOT NULL
      AND pcn <> ''

    UNION

    SELECT DISTINCT
        TRIM(UPPER(pcn)) AS pcn_id
    FROM {{ ref('popla_code_deleted') }}
    WHERE pcn IS NOT NULL
      AND pcn <> ''

),

popla_case_ranked AS (

    SELECT
        pcn_id,
        popla_opened_date,
        case_schedule_date,
        evidence_date,
        email_alert,
        alert2,

        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY pcn_id
            ORDER BY popla_opened_date DESC
        ) AS row_num

    FROM {{ ref('core_popla_case_legacy') }}

),

popla_case_latest AS (

    SELECT
        pcn_id,
        popla_opened_date,
        case_schedule_date,
        evidence_date,
        email_alert,
        alert2

    FROM popla_case_ranked
    WHERE row_num = 1

),

cancelled_popla_lost AS (

    SELECT DISTINCT
        TRIM(UPPER(pcn)) AS pcn_id
    FROM {{ ref('cancelled') }}
    WHERE reason = 'POPLA lost'

),

cancelled_popla AS (

    SELECT DISTINCT
        TRIM(UPPER(pcn)) AS pcn_id
    FROM {{ ref('cancelled') }}
    WHERE reason = 'POPLA'

),

violators_popla_status AS (

    SELECT DISTINCT
        TRIM(UPPER(full_pcn)) AS pcn_id
    FROM {{ ref('violators') }}
    WHERE pcn_status = 'Popla'

),

email_cancellation AS (

    SELECT DISTINCT
        TRIM(UPPER(pcn)) AS pcn_id
    FROM {{ ref('email_appeal_log') }}
    WHERE email_type = 'cancellation'

),

email_exhausted AS (

    SELECT DISTINCT
        TRIM(UPPER(pcn)) AS pcn_id
    FROM {{ ref('email_appeal_log') }}
    WHERE email_type IN (
        'Exhaustion Letter',
        'Unpaid PCN withdrawn at POPLA stage'
    )

),

cancelled_dated AS (

    SELECT
        TRIM(UPPER(pcn)) AS pcn_id,
        cancelled        AS cancelled_date
    FROM {{ ref('cancelled') }}
    WHERE cancelled IS NOT NULL

),

violators_escalated AS (

    SELECT
        TRIM(UPPER(full_pcn)) AS pcn_id,
        pcn_status_updated

    FROM {{ ref('violators') }}

    WHERE pcn_status IN (
        '1st Reminder',
        '2nd Reminder',
        'Third Reminder',
        'nonpofa2reminder',
        'lbareminder',
        'postccj14daysreminder',
        'LBA',
        'lba',
        'debtrecovery',
        'debtrecvoerypostccj',
        'drreturned',
        'drreturnedpostccj',
        'Debt Recovery Failed Installment',
        'debtrecoverycancelled',
        'Debt Recovery Failed Installment Returned'
    )

      AND pcn_status_updated IS NOT NULL

),

legacy_appeals_lifecycle AS (

    SELECT
        ca.appeal_id,
        ca.pcn_id,
        ca.appeal_type,
        CAST(ca.submitted_date AS DATE) AS submitted_date,
        ca.appeal_reason,

        ca.status_candidate_a AS appeal_stage,

        CAST(ca.submitted_date AS DATE)
            AS appeal_stage_start_date,

        ca.status_candidate_b AS appeal_admin_status,

        CAST(
            CASE
                WHEN pcf.pcn_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1
                ELSE 0
            END
            AS BIT
        ) AS popla_appeal_flag,

        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(100))
            AS popla_appeal_status,

        CAST(pcl.popla_opened_date AS DATE)
            AS popla_appeal_start_date,

        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(100))
            AS popla_appeal_stage,

        CAST(
            COALESCE(
                TRY_CAST(pcl.case_schedule_date AS DATETIME2(6)),
                TRY_CAST(pcl.evidence_date AS DATETIME2(6)),
                TRY_CAST(pcl.popla_opened_date AS DATETIME2(6))
            )
            AS DATE
        ) AS popla_appeal_stage_start_date,

        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(500))
            AS popla_appeal_stage_reason,

        CAST(NULL AS INT)
            AS appeal_age_days,

        CASE
            WHEN cpl.pcn_id IS NOT NULL
                THEN 'UPHELD_AT_POPLA'

            WHEN cp.pcn_id IS NOT NULL
              OR vps.pcn_id IS NOT NULL
                THEN 'POPLA_STAGE'

            WHEN ec.pcn_id IS NOT NULL
              OR EXISTS (
                    SELECT 1
                    FROM cancelled_dated cd
                    WHERE cd.pcn_id = ca.pcn_id
                      AND cd.cancelled_date > ca.submitted_date
                )
                THEN 'UPHELD'

            WHEN ee.pcn_id IS NOT NULL
                THEN 'REJECTED_FINAL'

            WHEN EXISTS (
                    SELECT 1
                    FROM violators_escalated ve
                    WHERE ve.pcn_id = ca.pcn_id
                      AND ve.pcn_status_updated > ca.submitted_date
                )
                THEN 'REJECTED'

            ELSE NULL
        END AS appeal_final_outcome,

        CAST(df.discount_flag AS BIT)
            AS discount_applied_flag,

        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(100))
            AS admin_status

    FROM {{ ref('core_appeal_legacy') }} ca

    LEFT JOIN popla_code_flag pcf
        ON pcf.pcn_id = ca.pcn_id

    LEFT JOIN popla_case_latest pcl
        ON pcl.pcn_id = ca.pcn_id

    LEFT JOIN cancelled_popla_lost cpl
        ON cpl.pcn_id = ca.pcn_id

    LEFT JOIN cancelled_popla cp
        ON cp.pcn_id = ca.pcn_id

    LEFT JOIN violators_popla_status vps
        ON vps.pcn_id = ca.pcn_id

    LEFT JOIN email_cancellation ec
        ON ec.pcn_id = ca.pcn_id

    LEFT JOIN email_exhausted ee
        ON ee.pcn_id = ca.pcn_id

    LEFT JOIN {{ ref('int_discount_flag_legacy') }} df
        ON df.pcn_id = ca.pcn_id

)

SELECT
    appeal_id,
    pcn_id,
    appeal_type,
    submitted_date,
    appeal_reason,
    appeal_stage,
    appeal_stage_start_date,
    appeal_admin_status,
    popla_appeal_flag,
    popla_appeal_status,
    popla_appeal_start_date,
    popla_appeal_stage,
    popla_appeal_stage_start_date,
    popla_appeal_stage_reason,
    appeal_age_days,
    appeal_final_outcome,
    discount_applied_flag,
    admin_status

FROM legacy_appeals_lifecycle

model.ccp.core_appeal_legacy.name: core_appeal_legacy
model.ccp.core_appeal_legacy.raw_code:
-- Core appeal entity (Built from Traffic Guard violators_appeal, ALONE).
-- Grain = 1 per appeal (violators_appeal.id, ~775,975 rows -- the online-
-- portal era). Per the TrafficGuard appeals domain build spec (2026-08-18).
--
-- Naming: TrafficGuard/NewLogic (legacy-system) core entity -- see the naming
-- note in core_claim_legacy.sql.
--
-- IMPORTANT: `appeals` (326,504 rows) is NOT an appeals table -- it's a
-- contact/call log (61% telephony outcomes: Spoken/Left Message/Unavailable/
-- No Answer, plus "duplicate message"/"other"). Its outcome/action columns
-- do NOT belong in this entity or feed appeal_final_outcome/
-- discount_applied_flag directly -- those are derived in fact_appeals_legacy
-- from cancelled/violators.pcnstatus/emailappeallog/pcnticketpricelog
-- instead. This entity anchors on violators_appeal alone.
--
-- PCN resolution: violators_id -> violators.ID (99.998% match) ONLY.
-- NEVER fall back to the appeal's own `pcn` text column (88.7% match) --
-- pcn_id is left NULL on the ~0.002% that don't resolve via ID.
--
-- Two candidate "stage" fields are carried through under neutral names,
-- unmapped -- which maps to appeal_stage vs appeal_admin_status is an open
-- business decision (see fact_appeals_legacy.sql header), not something to
-- guess here.

{{ config(
    alias = 'core_appeal_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'appeals']
) }}

WITH

base AS (
    SELECT
        id                          AS appeal_sk,
        id                          AS appeal_id,
        violators_id                AS violator_sk,
        appeal_as                   AS appeal_type,
        reason_for_appeal_ext       AS appeal_reason,
        created_at                  AS submitted_date,
        updated_at                  AS last_updated_at,
        evidence_merge_status       AS status_candidate_a,
        copy_to_server_status       AS status_candidate_b
    FROM {{ ref('violators_appeal') }}
),

violator_lookup AS (
    SELECT
        id                          AS violator_sk,
        TRIM(UPPER(full_pcn))       AS pcn_id
    FROM {{ ref('violators') }}
)

SELECT
    b.appeal_sk,
    b.appeal_id,
    vl.pcn_id,
    b.violator_sk,
    b.appeal_type,
    b.appeal_reason,
    b.submitted_date,
    b.last_updated_at,
    b.status_candidate_a,
    b.status_candidate_b

FROM base b
LEFT JOIN violator_lookup vl ON vl.violator_sk = b.violator_sk

model.ccp.core_appeal_letter_para_legacy.name: core_appeal_letter_para_legacy
model.ccp.core_appeal_letter_para_legacy.raw_code:
-- Core appeal letter-paragraph bridge (Built from Traffic Guard
-- appealletterpara + appealletters + appealpara). Grain = 1 per
-- letter-paragraph pair (~951,980 rows). Per the TrafficGuard appeals
-- domain build spec (2026-08-18, confirmed-linkage revision).
--
-- Naming: TrafficGuard/NewLogic (legacy-system) core entity -- see the naming
-- note in core_claim_legacy.sql.
--
-- CONFIRMED CHAIN (verified live, both by the spec's own measurement and
-- independently re-checked here: 924,289/951,980 = 97.1%):
--   appealletterpara.appealid     -> appealletters.id       97.1%
--   appealletters.violatorid      -> violators.ID           99.7%
--   appealletterpara.appealparaid -> appealpara.id
-- An earlier test wrongly paired appealid against violators_appeal.id
-- directly (0/33,403 agreements) -- that was testing the wrong columns, not
-- evidence the linkage doesn't exist. See dbt_project.yml note.
--
-- FAN-OUT: a letter averages 2.02 paragraphs (max 45) -- this model is the
-- full bridge grain. See core_appeal_reason_legacy.sql for the collapsed
-- one-row-per-violator view that's safe to join into a fact.
--
-- is_discount_para: appeal_para_id = 162 is THE £20-discount paragraph,
-- confirmed by direct lookup + usage count (45,370 uses, exact match to
-- the build spec's figure).
--
-- Per context.md §9 rule 1, the pcn-shaped key is TRIM/UPPER-normalised.

{{ config(
    alias = 'core_appeal_letter_para_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'appeals']
) }}

WITH

letters AS (
    SELECT
        id             AS letter_id,
        violator_id,
        date           AS letter_date
    FROM {{ ref('appeal_letters') }}
),

violator_lookup AS (
    SELECT
        id                        AS violator_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(full_pcn))     AS pcn_id
    FROM {{ ref('violators') }}
)

SELECT
    l.letter_id,
    l.violator_id       AS violator_sk,
    vl.pcn_id,
    alp.appeal_para_id,
    ap.ref               AS para_ref,
    ap.short_paragraph   AS para_short_text,
    CAST(CASE WHEN alp.appeal_para_id = 162 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS BIT) AS is_discount_para,
    l.letter_date

FROM {{ ref('appeal_letter_para') }} alp
LEFT JOIN letters l             ON l.letter_id = alp.appeal_id  -- 97.1% match; LEFT to keep the full 951,980-row grain
LEFT JOIN violator_lookup vl    ON vl.violator_id = l.violator_id
LEFT JOIN {{ ref('appeal_para') }} ap ON ap.id = alp.appeal_para_id

model.ccp.core_appeal_reason_legacy.name: core_appeal_reason_legacy
model.ccp.core_appeal_reason_legacy.raw_code:
-- Core appeal reason (collapsed) -- one row per violator, picking a single
-- primary rejection-reason paragraph out of core_appeal_letter_para_legacy's
-- full bridge grain. Per the TrafficGuard appeals domain build spec
-- (2026-08-18, confirmed-linkage revision).
--
-- Naming: TrafficGuard/NewLogic (legacy-system) core entity -- see the naming
-- note in core_claim_legacy.sql.
--
-- Grain is VIOLATOR, not appeal -- the source chain (appealletterpara ->
-- appealletters -> violators) resolves to a violator/PCN, not to a specific
-- violators_appeal row. If a violator has multiple appeals, they all see the
-- same reason. This is the "safe to join into a fact" view the build spec
-- calls for -- fact_appeals_legacy joins it via violator_sk.
--
-- Primary-paragraph tiebreak: highest global usage across the whole bridge
-- wins; ties broken by lowest appeal_para_id. Coverage is 51.5% of appealed
-- violators per the build spec (354,832 of 688,672) -- the rest are
-- genuinely null, not a defect, and should not be backfilled.

{{ config(
    alias = 'core_appeal_reason_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'appeals']
) }}

WITH

para_usage AS (
    SELECT appeal_para_id, COUNT(*) AS usage_count
    FROM {{ ref('core_appeal_letter_para_legacy') }}
    WHERE appeal_para_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY appeal_para_id
),

ranked AS (
    SELECT
        lp.violator_sk,
        lp.pcn_id,
        lp.appeal_para_id,
        lp.para_ref,
        lp.para_short_text,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY lp.violator_sk
            ORDER BY pu.usage_count DESC, lp.appeal_para_id ASC
        ) AS rn
    FROM {{ ref('core_appeal_letter_para_legacy') }} lp
    LEFT JOIN para_usage pu ON pu.appeal_para_id = lp.appeal_para_id
    WHERE lp.violator_sk IS NOT NULL
      AND lp.appeal_para_id IS NOT NULL
),

-- Independent of the primary-paragraph tiebreak above: was the discount
-- paragraph used ANYWHERE among this violator's letters, not just as
-- whichever paragraph happens to be picked as "primary".
discount_flag AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT violator_sk
    FROM {{ ref('core_appeal_letter_para_legacy') }}
    WHERE is_discount_para = 1
)

SELECT
    r.violator_sk,
    r.pcn_id,
    r.appeal_para_id       AS appeal_id,
    r.para_ref             AS primary_para_ref,
    r.para_short_text      AS appeal_reason,
    CAST(CASE WHEN df.violator_sk IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS BIT) AS has_discount_para
FROM ranked r
LEFT JOIN discount_flag df ON df.violator_sk = r.violator_sk
WHERE r.rn = 1

model.ccp.core_popla_case_legacy.name: core_popla_case_legacy
model.ccp.core_popla_case_legacy.raw_code:
-- Core POPLA case entity (Built from Traffic Guard tbPopla, enriched with
-- poplacode + poplacodedeleted). Grain = 1 per POPLA case (tbPopla.id,
-- ~56,178 rows). Per the TrafficGuard appeals domain build spec (2026-08-18).
--
-- Naming: TrafficGuard/NewLogic (legacy-system) core entity -- see the naming
-- note in core_claim_legacy.sql.
--
-- ⚠️ popla_appeal_flag (built from this + poplacode/poplacodedeleted
-- existence in fact_appeals_legacy) has a 58.4% existence ratio against
-- appeals -- implausibly high for what should be a rare escalation.
-- Provisional, not a settled signal, pending business sanity check.
--
-- popla_code is the latest poplacode/poplacodedeleted record per pcn, with
-- popla_code_source flagging which of the two tables it came from (the
-- build spec: "union the two, flag which").

{{ config(
    alias = 'core_popla_case_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'appeals']
) }}

WITH

base AS (
    SELECT
        id                      AS popla_sk,
        TRIM(UPPER(pcn))        AS pcn_id,
        case_number,
        case_schedule_date,
        evidence_date,
        date_added              AS popla_opened_date,
        email_alert,
        alert_2                 AS alert2
    FROM {{ ref('tb_popla') }}
    WHERE pcn IS NOT NULL
      AND pcn <> ''
),

popla_code_union AS (
    SELECT pcn, code, date_inserted, 'poplacode'        AS popla_code_source FROM {{ ref('popla_code') }}
    UNION ALL
    SELECT pcn, code, date_inserted, 'poplacodedeleted'  AS popla_code_source FROM {{ ref('popla_code_deleted') }}
),

popla_code_ranked AS (
    SELECT
        TRIM(UPPER(pcn))    AS pcn_id,
        code                AS popla_code,
        popla_code_source,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY TRIM(UPPER(pcn))
            ORDER BY date_inserted DESC
        ) AS rn
    FROM popla_code_union
    WHERE pcn IS NOT NULL AND pcn <> ''
),

popla_code_latest AS (
    SELECT pcn_id, popla_code, popla_code_source
    FROM popla_code_ranked
    WHERE rn = 1
)

SELECT
    b.popla_sk,
    b.pcn_id,
    b.case_number,
    b.case_schedule_date,
    b.evidence_date,
    b.popla_opened_date,
    b.email_alert,
    b.alert2,
    pc.popla_code,
    pc.popla_code_source

FROM base b
LEFT JOIN popla_code_latest pc ON pc.pcn_id = b.pcn_id

model.ccp.core_camera_legacy.name: core_camera_legacy
model.ccp.core_camera_legacy.raw_code:
-- Core camera entity (Built from Traffic Guard newcsv_camera + secondary
-- anprceomonitor_cameras, UNIONed with a source_table discriminator).
-- Grain = 1 per camera installation (445 + 22 per context.md §7.12).
-- Per context.md §6.2 core__camera.
--
-- Naming: TrafficGuard/NewLogic (legacy-system) core entity -- see the naming
-- note in core_claim_legacy.sql.
--
-- camera_status only comes from newcsv_camera.state (3 values) -- do NOT use
-- anprceomonitor_cameras.ip_1_status/ip_2_status, both confirmed constant
-- (context.md §6.2/§9 rule 2 "populated but constant" list). Emitted as
-- explicit NULL for that source instead of a meaningless constant.
--
-- anprceomonitor_cameras.created_at is stored as free text (not datetime2)
-- in the source -- TRY_CAST rather than risking a bad cast.

{{ config(
    alias = 'core_camera_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'camera']
) }}

WITH

newcsv_channel AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('newcsv-', CAST(id AS VARCHAR(20)))     AS camera_installation_id,
        {{ pcn_key('site_id') }}                        AS site_id,
        camera_name                                      AS camera_id,
        created_at                                        AS camera_installation_date,
        state                                              AS camera_status,
        'newcsv_camera'                                    AS source_table
    FROM {{ ref('new_csv_camera') }}
),

anprceomonitor_channel AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('anprceomonitor-', CAST(id AS VARCHAR(20))) AS camera_installation_id,
        {{ pcn_key('site_id') }}                            AS site_id,
        camera_name                                          AS camera_id,
        TRY_CAST(created_at AS DATETIME2(6))                AS camera_installation_date,
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))                           AS camera_status,
        'anprceomonitor_cameras'                             AS source_table
    FROM {{ ref('anprceomonitor_cameras') }}
)

SELECT * FROM newcsv_channel
UNION ALL SELECT * FROM anprceomonitor_channel

model.ccp.core_claim_legacy.name: core_claim_legacy
model.ccp.core_claim_legacy.raw_code:
/*
Model Description :
    - Core claim entity built from Traffic Guard court_issued plus claims-domain enrichment and decoded attributes.
    - Grain: One row per court claim: court_issued.id.
    - Important payment definitions:
        - total_paid: PCN-level derived amount passed through from core_pcn_legacy.
        - post_court_cash_collected: Actual payment amount received on or after claim_issue_date.
    - PCNs are business identifiers and must remain VARCHAR throughout. They must never be implicitly or explicitly converted to INT.

Created On : 09-17-2026
*/


{{ config(
    alias = 'core_claim_legacy',
    tags  = ['core', 'claims']
) }}

WITH 

-- ========================================================================
-- 1. IMPORT CTEs
-- ========================================================================

src_court_issued               AS ( SELECT * FROM {{ ref('court_issued') }} ),
src_violators                  AS ( SELECT * FROM {{ ref('violators') }} ),
src_court_issued_status        AS ( SELECT * FROM {{ ref('court_issued_status') }} ),
src_pcn_claim_status           AS ( SELECT * FROM {{ ref('pcn_claim_status') }} ),
src_judgement_notice           AS ( SELECT * FROM {{ ref('judgement_notice') }} ),
src_defense                    AS ( SELECT * FROM {{ ref('defense') }} ),
src_court_hearings             AS ( SELECT * FROM {{ ref('court_hearings') }} ),
src_debt_recovery_post_ccj     AS ( SELECT * FROM {{ ref('debt_recovery_post_ccj') }} ),
src_failed_instalment_claim    AS ( SELECT * FROM {{ ref('failed_instalment_claim') }} ),
src_failed_instalment_post_ccj AS ( SELECT * FROM {{ ref('failed_instalment_post_ccj') }} ),
src_payments                   AS ( SELECT * FROM {{ ref('payments') }} ),
src_ccp_tickettransaction      AS ( SELECT * FROM {{ ref('ccp_tickettransaction') }} ),
src_int_incident_deduped       AS ( SELECT * FROM {{ ref('int_incident_deduped') }} ),
src_courtissued_status_map     AS ( SELECT * FROM {{ ref('courtissued_status_map') }} ),
src_core_pcn_legacy            AS ( SELECT * FROM {{ ref('core_pcn_legacy') }} ),
src_int_claim_type_legacy      AS ( SELECT * FROM {{ ref('int_claim_type_legacy') }} ),

-- ========================================================================
-- 2. STANDARDIZATION & PREP CTEs
-- ========================================================================

base AS (
    SELECT
        id AS claim_id
        , TRIM(UPPER(CAST(pcn AS VARCHAR(50)))) AS claim_pcn
        , COALESCE(date_claim_obtained, datetime) AS claim_issue_date
        , claim_type AS claim_handling_route
        , court_issued_status
        , date_claim_obtained AS claim_stage_start_date
        , date_judgement_obtained AS ccj_date
        , CAST(
            CASE
                WHEN confirmed_ccj IS NOT NULL THEN 1
                ELSE 0
            END AS BIT
        ) AS ccj_confirmed_flag
    FROM 
        src_court_issued AS ci
    WHERE 
        ci.pcn IS NOT NULL
        AND TRIM(CAST(ci.pcn AS VARCHAR(50))) <> ''
        AND EXISTS (
            SELECT 1
            FROM src_violators v
            WHERE TRIM(UPPER(CAST(v.full_pcn AS VARCHAR(50)))) = TRIM(UPPER(CAST(ci.pcn AS VARCHAR(50))))
              AND v.claim IS NOT NULL
        )
),

claim_status_decode AS (
    SELECT
        id
        , status AS claim_status
    FROM 
        src_court_issued_status
),

claim_stage_ranked AS (
    SELECT
        TRIM(UPPER(CAST(pcn AS VARCHAR(50)))) AS claim_pcn
        , claim_status                        AS claim_stage_supplementary
        , date_added
        , ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY TRIM(UPPER(CAST(pcn AS VARCHAR(50))))
            ORDER BY date_added DESC
        ) AS rn
    FROM 
        src_pcn_claim_status
    WHERE 
        pcn IS NOT NULL
        AND TRIM(CAST(pcn AS VARCHAR(50))) <> ''
),

claim_stage_latest AS (
    SELECT
        claim_pcn
        , claim_stage_supplementary
    FROM 
        claim_stage_ranked
    WHERE 
        rn = 1
),

judgement_notice_ranked AS (
    SELECT
        TRIM(UPPER(CAST(pcn AS VARCHAR(50)))) AS claim_pcn
        , judgement_type
        , claims_stayed
        , court                               AS judgement_court
        , ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY TRIM(UPPER(CAST(pcn AS VARCHAR(50))))
            ORDER BY id DESC
        ) AS rn
    FROM 
        src_judgement_notice
    WHERE 
        pcn IS NOT NULL
        AND TRIM(CAST(pcn AS VARCHAR(50))) <> ''
),

judgement_notice_latest AS (
    SELECT
        claim_pcn
        , judgement_type
        , claims_stayed
        , judgement_court
    FROM 
        judgement_notice_ranked
    WHERE 
        rn = 1
),

defense_ranked AS (
    SELECT
        TRIM(UPPER(CAST(pcn AS VARCHAR(50)))) AS claim_pcn
        , court                               AS defense_court
        , ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY TRIM(UPPER(CAST(pcn AS VARCHAR(50))))
            ORDER BY [date] DESC
        ) AS rn
    FROM 
        src_defense
    WHERE 
        pcn IS NOT NULL
        AND TRIM(CAST(pcn AS VARCHAR(50))) <> ''
),

defense_latest AS (
    SELECT
        claim_pcn
        , defense_court
    FROM 
        defense_ranked
    WHERE 
        rn = 1
),

court_hearing AS (
    SELECT
        TRIM(UPPER(CAST(claim AS VARCHAR(100)))) AS court_claim_number
        , MAX(court)                             AS hearing_court
        , COUNT_BIG(*)                           AS hearing_count
        , MIN(
            TRY_CAST(
                RIGHT([date], 4) + '-' + SUBSTRING([date], 4, 2) + '-' + LEFT([date], 2)
                AS DATE
            )
        )                                        AS court_hearing_date
        , MIN(
            TRY_CAST(
                RIGHT(date_of_hearing, 4) + '-' + SUBSTRING(date_of_hearing, 4, 2) + '-' + LEFT(date_of_hearing, 2)
                AS DATE
            )
        )                                        AS court_hearing_scheduled_date
    FROM 
        src_court_hearings
    WHERE 
        claim IS NOT NULL
        AND TRIM(CAST(claim AS VARCHAR(100))) <> ''
    GROUP BY
        TRIM(UPPER(CAST(claim AS VARCHAR(100))))
),

post_ccj_recovery_ranked AS (
    SELECT
        TRIM(UPPER(CAST(pcn AS VARCHAR(50)))) AS claim_pcn
        , dr_type
        , ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY TRIM(UPPER(CAST(pcn AS VARCHAR(50))))
            ORDER BY id DESC
        ) AS rn
    FROM 
        src_debt_recovery_post_ccj
    WHERE 
        pcn IS NOT NULL
        AND TRIM(CAST(pcn AS VARCHAR(50))) <> ''
),

post_ccj_recovery_latest AS (
    SELECT
        claim_pcn
        , dr_type AS post_ccj_recovery_type
    FROM 
        post_ccj_recovery_ranked
    WHERE 
        rn = 1
),

failed_instalment_claim_flag AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        TRIM(UPPER(CAST(pcn AS VARCHAR(50)))) AS claim_pcn
    FROM 
        src_failed_instalment_claim
    WHERE 
        pcn IS NOT NULL
        AND TRIM(CAST(pcn AS VARCHAR(50))) <> ''
),

failed_instalment_post_ccj_flag AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        TRIM(UPPER(CAST(pcn AS VARCHAR(50)))) AS claim_pcn
    FROM 
        src_failed_instalment_post_ccj
    WHERE 
        pcn IS NOT NULL
        AND TRIM(CAST(pcn AS VARCHAR(50))) <> ''
),

payment_source AS (
    SELECT
        id                                    AS payment_id
        , TRIM(UPPER(CAST(pcn AS VARCHAR(50)))) AS claim_pcn
        , CAST(amount AS DECIMAL(19,4))       AS payment_amount
        , received                            AS payment_date
    FROM 
        src_payments
    WHERE 
        pcn IS NOT NULL
        AND TRIM(CAST(pcn AS VARCHAR(50))) <> ''
        AND amount IS NOT NULL
        AND amount <> 0
),

zeus_payment_source AS (
    SELECT
        t.ccp_tickettransactionid                           AS payment_id
        , TRIM(UPPER(CAST(i.ccp_ticketno AS VARCHAR(50))))  AS claim_pcn
        , CAST(t.ccp_amount AS DECIMAL(19,4))               AS payment_amount
        , CAST(t.ccp_transactiondate AS DATE)               AS payment_date
    FROM 
        src_ccp_tickettransaction t
    JOIN 
        src_int_incident_deduped i ON LOWER(t.ccp_ticket) = LOWER(i.incidentid)
    WHERE 
        t.ccp_transactiontype = 860620000
        AND i.ccp_ticketno IS NOT NULL
),

combined_payment_source AS (
    SELECT payment_id, claim_pcn, payment_amount, payment_date FROM payment_source
    
    UNION ALL
    
    SELECT payment_id, claim_pcn, payment_amount, payment_date FROM zeus_payment_source
),

post_court_payments_by_claim AS (
    SELECT
        b.claim_id
        , SUM(pay.payment_amount)   AS post_court_cash_collected
        , COUNT_BIG(*)              AS post_court_payment_count
        , MIN(pay.payment_date)     AS first_post_court_payment_date
        , MAX(pay.payment_date)     AS last_post_court_payment_date
    FROM 
        base b
    INNER JOIN 
        combined_payment_source pay ON pay.claim_pcn = b.claim_pcn AND pay.payment_date >= b.claim_issue_date
    GROUP BY
        b.claim_id
),

-- ========================================================================
-- 3. FINAL INTEGRATION
-- ========================================================================

final AS (
    SELECT
        b.claim_id
        , b.claim_pcn
        , p.site_id
        , p.court_claim_number
        , b.claim_issue_date
        , b.claim_handling_route
        , ct.claim_type
        , ct.pcn_count
        , csd.claim_status
        , cst.claim_stage_supplementary
        , b.claim_stage_start_date
        , CASE
            WHEN dl.claim_pcn IS NOT NULL THEN 1
            ELSE 0
          END                                             AS defended_status
        , CAST(
            CASE
                WHEN ch.court_claim_number IS NOT NULL THEN 1
                ELSE 0
            END AS BIT
          )                                               AS court_flag
        , COALESCE(
            jn.judgement_court,
            dl.defense_court,
            ch.hearing_court
        ) AS court_type,

        jn.judgement_type,
        jn.claims_stayed,

        b.ccj_date,

        csm.ccj_state AS ccj_status,
        csm.ccj_state_order AS ccj_status_order,

        b.ccj_confirmed_flag,

        ch.court_hearing_date,
        ch.court_hearing_scheduled_date,
        ch.hearing_count,

        -- PCN-level attributes inherited from core_pcn_legacy.
        p.payment_status,
        p.issue_date AS pcn_issue_date,

        p.charge AS claim_amount,

        p.fully_paid_flag,

        -- PCN-level derived amount.
        -- Kept for comparison but not used as Post Court Cash Collected.
        p.total_paid,

        CAST(
            CASE
                WHEN COALESCE(p.total_paid, CAST(0 AS DECIMAL(19,4))) > 0 THEN 1
                ELSE 0
            END AS BIT
          )                                               AS total_paid_flag
        , CASE
            WHEN pccj.claim_pcn IS NOT NULL THEN 'Sent'
            ELSE NULL
          END                                             AS post_ccj_recovery_status
        , pccj.post_ccj_recovery_type
        , CAST(
            COALESCE(pay.post_court_cash_collected, CAST(0 AS DECIMAL(19,4))) AS DECIMAL(19,4)
          )                                               AS post_court_cash_collected
        , CAST(
            CASE
                WHEN COALESCE(pay.post_court_payment_count, 0) > 0 THEN 1
                ELSE 0
            END AS BIT
          )                                               AS post_court_cash_collected_flag
        , COALESCE(pay.post_court_payment_count, CAST(0 AS BIGINT)) AS post_court_payment_count
        , pay.first_post_court_payment_date
        , pay.last_post_court_payment_date
        , CASE
            WHEN fic.claim_pcn IS NOT NULL OR fipc.claim_pcn IS NOT NULL THEN 'Failed'
            ELSE NULL
          END                                             AS instalment_status

    FROM 
        base b
    LEFT JOIN 
        claim_status_decode csd ON csd.id = b.court_issued_status
    LEFT JOIN 
        src_courtissued_status_map csm ON csm.status_id = b.court_issued_status
    LEFT JOIN 
        claim_stage_latest cst ON CAST(cst.claim_pcn AS VARCHAR(50)) = CAST(b.claim_pcn AS VARCHAR(50))
    LEFT JOIN 
        judgement_notice_latest jn ON CAST(jn.claim_pcn AS VARCHAR(50)) = CAST(b.claim_pcn AS VARCHAR(50))
    LEFT JOIN 
        defense_latest dl ON CAST(dl.claim_pcn AS VARCHAR(50)) = CAST(b.claim_pcn AS VARCHAR(50))
    LEFT JOIN 
        src_core_pcn_legacy p ON CAST(p.pcn_id AS VARCHAR(50)) = CAST(b.claim_pcn AS VARCHAR(50))
    LEFT JOIN 
        court_hearing ch ON CAST(ch.court_claim_number AS VARCHAR(100)) = TRIM(UPPER(CAST(p.court_claim_number AS VARCHAR(100))))
    LEFT JOIN 
        src_int_claim_type_legacy ct ON CAST(ct.pcn_id AS VARCHAR(50)) = CAST(b.claim_pcn AS VARCHAR(50))
    LEFT JOIN 
        post_ccj_recovery_latest pccj ON CAST(pccj.claim_pcn AS VARCHAR(50)) = CAST(b.claim_pcn AS VARCHAR(50))
    LEFT JOIN 
        failed_instalment_claim_flag fic ON CAST(fic.claim_pcn AS VARCHAR(50)) = CAST(b.claim_pcn AS VARCHAR(50))
    LEFT JOIN 
        post_court_payments_by_claim pay ON pay.claim_id = b.claim_id
    LEFT JOIN 
        failed_instalment_post_ccj_flag fipc ON CAST(fipc.claim_pcn AS VARCHAR(50)) = CAST(b.claim_pcn AS VARCHAR(50))
)

SELECT * FROM final

model.ccp.core_court_legacy.name: core_court_legacy
model.ccp.core_court_legacy.raw_code:
-- Core court reference (Built from Traffic Guard `courts`).
-- Grain = 1 per court. Standalone -- no site or PCN link exists in the source;
-- claims reference courts by NAME only (judgementnotice.court / courthearings.court
-- / defense.court, all heavily null -- see core_claim_legacy). Feeds
-- core_claim_legacy (court name resolution) and, eventually, dim_court.
-- context.md §6.5 / §8.
--
-- Naming: TrafficGuard/NewLogic (legacy-system) core entity -- see the naming
-- note in core_claim_legacy.sql.
--
-- `court_id` is a normalised (TRIM/UPPER) version of court_name, since the
-- source has no numeric court key -- context.md §9 rule 1.

{{ config(
    alias = 'core_court_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'claims']
) }}

WITH

ranked AS (
    SELECT
        TRIM(UPPER(court_name))    AS court_id,
        court_name,
        court_address_line_1,
        court_address_line_11,
        court_address_line_12,
        postcode,
        phone,
        email,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY TRIM(UPPER(court_name))
            ORDER BY court_name
        ) AS rn
    FROM {{ ref('courts') }}
    WHERE court_name IS NOT NULL
      AND court_name <> ''
)

SELECT
    court_id,
    court_name,
    court_address_line_1,
    court_address_line_11,
    court_address_line_12,
    postcode,
    phone,
    email
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1

model.ccp.core_client_legacy.name: core_client_legacy
model.ccp.core_client_legacy.raw_code:
-- Core client entity (Built from Traffic Guard clients, enriched with
-- clientadminsites for a site count). Grain = 1 per client. Per context.md
-- §6.1 core__customer.
--
-- Naming: TrafficGuard/NewLogic (legacy-system) core entity -- see the naming
-- note in core_claim_legacy.sql.
--
-- RENAMED from core_customer_legacy.sql (2026-08-31, dbt build guide --
-- dimension tables, second pass) to core_client_legacy -- the client's
-- second-pass ERD calls this entity "client", not "customer", and
-- dim_customer_legacy is renamed to dim_client_legacy to match. Only this
-- entity's own output column names change (customer_id/customer_name ->
-- client_id/client_name); core_site_legacy's FK column into this entity is
-- deliberately left as `customer_id` (3 downstream facts already consume it
-- -- fact_site_lifecycle_legacy, fact_site_status_legacy, core_site_lifecycle
-- _legacy -- renaming it would ripple into files unrelated to this pass).
--
-- clients has only 2 columns (clientid, clientname) -- status/postcode/
-- state/country have no source anywhere (context.md §8 dim_customer), not
-- reproduced here as NULLs since nothing downstream currently consumes them
-- from this entity; dim_client_legacy adds them as typed NULLs instead.

{{ config(
    alias = 'core_client_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'customer']
) }}

WITH

site_counts AS (
    SELECT client_id, COUNT(DISTINCT {{ pcn_key('site_code') }}) AS site_count
    FROM {{ ref('client_admin_sites') }}
    GROUP BY client_id
)

SELECT
    c.client_id     AS client_id,
    c.client_name   AS client_name,
    sc.site_count

FROM {{ ref('clients') }} c
LEFT JOIN site_counts sc ON sc.client_id = c.client_id

model.ccp.core_dvla_review_legacy.name: core_dvla_review_legacy
model.ccp.core_dvla_review_legacy.raw_code:
-- Core DVLA review entity (Built from Traffic Guard dvla, enriched with
-- dvlarep + dvlabatches/dvlaoverlimit). Grain = 1 per DVLA enquiry
-- (dvla.id anchor). Per context.md §6.3 core__dvla_review.
--
-- Naming: TrafficGuard/NewLogic (legacy-system) core entity -- see the naming
-- note in core_claim_legacy.sql.
--
-- Join to the PCN spine via violators.dvlaid -> dvla.ID (97.0%, primary per
-- context.md §4.1); Registration -> dvla.Reg (95.9%) is documented as a
-- fallback cross-check but not implemented as an actual fallback join here --
-- doing so would require a second, lower-confidence join path for a small
-- incremental gain, and risks double-counting if both paths disagree. Flagged
-- rather than silently added.
--
-- dvla_submission_batch_id here is dvlaBatches only (92.5% to dvla per
-- context.md) -- dvlarep/dvlaoverlimit's own batch match rates (70.3%/40.6%)
-- are weaker and not additionally unioned in.

{{ config(
    alias = 'core_dvla_review_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'dvla_review']
) }}

WITH

base AS (
    SELECT
        id                      AS dvla_review_id,
        reg                     AS vehicle_id,
        date_received           AS dvla_engine_date,
        type                    AS dvla_api_check_outcome_type,
        -- Hard copy is a DVLA RESPONSE STATE: the keeper details arrive by
        -- post rather than over the API. It has nothing to do with reanalysis
        -- (client correction C1), and it now feeds dni_status. reanalysis_flag
        -- has no confirmed source and is emitted as a typed NULL below.
        hard_copy_indicator,
        -- The REAL foreign key from dvla to dvlarep -- see the join note below.
        dvla_rep_id,
        batch_id
    FROM {{ ref('dvla') }}
),

-- CORRECTED JOIN KEY. dvlarep.dvla is a REGISTRATION -- varchar(20), sitting
-- beside offence / site / pcn / offenceDate -- not a foreign key to dvla.ID.
-- The previous version joined dvlarep.dvla = CAST(dvla.ID AS VARCHAR(20)),
-- i.e. a number plate against a stringified integer, which cannot match. That
-- left dvla_engine_status, both API dates and dvla_api_check_outcome NULL on
-- every row of this model and of fact_dvla_review. The real FK is
-- dvla.dvlarepid -> dvlarep.id, and `id` is dvlarep's own primary key, so no
-- latest-row dedup is needed at all.
dvlarep_latest AS (
    SELECT
        id                          AS dvla_rep_id,
        dvla                        AS enquiry_registration,
        site                        AS enquiry_site,
        offence_date                AS enquiry_offence_date,
        type                        AS dvla_engine_status,
        date_generated              AS dvla_api_sent_date,
        dvla_rec                    AS dvla_api_received_date,
        violator                    AS dvla_api_check_outcome,
        esther_notes
    FROM {{ ref('dvla_rep') }}
    WHERE id IS NOT NULL
),

violator_lookup AS (
    SELECT
        dvla_id,
        {{ pcn_key('full_pcn') }}   AS pcn_id,
        {{ pcn_key('registration') }} AS registration,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY dvla_id
            ORDER BY date_added DESC
        ) AS rn
    FROM {{ ref('violators') }}
    WHERE dvla_id IS NOT NULL
),

violator_latest AS (
    SELECT dvla_id, pcn_id, registration
    FROM violator_lookup
    WHERE rn = 1
),

-- Repeat offender: the client-confirmed rule is the THIRD DVLA enquiry onwards
-- for a registration, built in int_repeat_offender_legacy over dvlarep. This
-- previously used the `repeat_offenders` table -- 4,099 rows over 1,082
-- registrations, against 159,171 under the confirmed rule. Rolled up to one
-- row per registration here, because that model is enquiry-grained.
repeat_offender_latest AS (
    SELECT reg, MAX(CAST(repeat_offender_status AS TINYINT)) AS repeat_offender_status
    FROM {{ ref('int_repeat_offender_legacy') }}
    GROUP BY reg
)

SELECT
    b.dvla_review_id,
    b.vehicle_id,
    v.pcn_id,
    b.dvla_engine_date,
    dr.dvla_engine_status,
    dr.dvla_api_sent_date,
    dr.dvla_api_received_date,
    b.dvla_api_check_outcome_type,
    b.batch_id                                 AS dvla_submission_batch_id,
    CAST(ISNULL(b.hard_copy_indicator, 0) AS BIT)     AS hard_copy_indicator,
    CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                 AS reanalysis_flag,
    dr.dvla_api_check_outcome,
    -- dvlarep.esthernotes is 99.96% null and is not a reason domain. Carried
    -- under its own name; dvla_engine_reason has no source on dvlarep, whose
    -- only other candidate, EnquiryCode, is 100% NULL.
    dr.esther_notes,
    CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(255))                        AS dvla_engine_reason,
    dr.enquiry_registration,
    dr.enquiry_site,
    dr.enquiry_offence_date,
    CAST(ISNULL(ro.repeat_offender_status, 0) AS BIT) AS repeat_offender_status

FROM base b
LEFT JOIN dvlarep_latest dr         ON dr.dvla_rep_id = b.dvla_rep_id
LEFT JOIN violator_latest v         ON v.dvla_id = b.dvla_review_id
LEFT JOIN repeat_offender_latest ro  ON ro.reg = {{ pcn_key('b.vehicle_id') }}

model.ccp.core_engineer_visit_legacy.name: core_engineer_visit_legacy
model.ccp.core_engineer_visit_legacy.raw_code:
-- Core engineer visit entity (Built from Traffic Guard engineervisits,
-- resolving site_id via siteissues). Grain = 1 per visit
-- (engineervisits.visit_id anchor). Per context.md §6.6 core__engineer_visit.
--
-- Naming: TrafficGuard/NewLogic (legacy-system) core entity -- see the naming
-- note in core_claim_legacy.sql.
--
-- site_id resolves via issue_id -> siteissues.id -> siteissues.site
-- (99.98% match per context.md §7.13) -- engineervisits carries no site
-- column of its own.

{{ config(
    alias = 'core_engineer_visit_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'engineer_visit']
) }}

SELECT
    ev.visit_id             AS engineer_visit_id,
    {{ pcn_key('si.site') }} AS site_id,
    ev.arrival_date         AS visit_date,
    ev.closed_date,
    ev.engineer_id

FROM {{ ref('engineer_visits') }} ev
LEFT JOIN {{ ref('site_issues') }} si ON si.id = ev.issue_id

model.ccp.core_fine_legacy.name: core_fine_legacy
model.ccp.core_fine_legacy.raw_code:
-- Core fine/tariff entity (Built from Traffic Guard tariff). Grain = 1 per
-- site-scoped price point. Per the dbt build guide for the 10
-- TrafficGuard/NewLogic dimension tables (2026-08-28).
--
-- Naming: TrafficGuard/NewLogic (legacy-system) core entity -- see the
-- naming note in core_claim_legacy.sql.
--
-- NOTE (flagged, not resolved here): the target dim's shape (fine_name,
-- description, active, start_date, end_date) reads like a fine-TYPE
-- taxonomy (e.g. "overstay", "no valid ticket"). dbo.Tariff is not that --
-- it's a site-scoped price point (ticket_price/reduced_amount per site,
-- no name/description/lifecycle fields at all). 5 of 7 dim_fine_legacy
-- columns are NULL by construction because this source doesn't carry that
-- concept, not because of a data gap -- worth confirming with the client
-- whether a price-point dimension is what's actually wanted here.

{{ config(
    alias = 'core_fine_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'fine']
) }}

SELECT
    id                  AS fine_id,
    ticket_price         AS amount,
    reduced_amount        AS amount_reduced   -- companion field, real and cheap to carry through core
FROM {{ ref('tariff') }}

model.ccp.int_appeal_outcome_legacy.name: int_appeal_outcome_legacy
model.ccp.int_appeal_outcome_legacy.raw_code:
-- Intermediate: appeal_final_outcome derivation (legacy/TrafficGuard).
-- Grain = 1 per appeal (same grain as core_appeal_legacy). Per context.md §4.3.
--
-- No stored outcome column exists anywhere in TrafficGuard -- derived by
-- precedence, first match wins. Never invent an 'UNKNOWN' value: an appeal
-- that matches none of the five tiers gets NULL, not a manufactured label.
--
-- email_signal is many-per-PCN (emailappeallog), so it is ranked by
-- precedence (MIN of the CASE below), not aggregated with MAX -- picking the
-- most-significant email type per PCN, not just any of them.

{{ config(
    alias = 'int_appeal_outcome_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'intermediate', 'appeals']
) }}

WITH email_signal AS (
    SELECT
        {{ pcn_key('pcn') }} AS pcn_id,
        MIN(CASE email_type
                WHEN 'Unpaid PCN withdrawn at POPLA stage' THEN 1
                WHEN 'Exhaustion Letter'                   THEN 2
                WHEN 'cancellation'                        THEN 3
                ELSE 99
            END) AS email_rank
    FROM {{ ref('email_appeal_log') }}
    GROUP BY {{ pcn_key('pcn') }}
),

cancel_signal AS (
    SELECT {{ pcn_key('pcn') }} AS pcn_id, MAX(reason) AS cancel_reason
    FROM {{ ref('cancelled') }}
    GROUP BY {{ pcn_key('pcn') }}
)

SELECT
    a.appeal_id,
    a.pcn_id,
    CASE
        WHEN c.cancel_reason = 'POPLA lost'                          THEN 'UPHELD_AT_POPLA'
        WHEN c.cancel_reason = 'POPLA' OR p.current_status = 'Popla' THEN 'POPLA_STAGE'
        WHEN e.email_rank = 3 OR p.cancelled_flag = 1                THEN 'UPHELD'
        WHEN e.email_rank IN (1, 2)                                  THEN 'REJECTED_FINAL'
        WHEN m.collection_cycle_stage_order > 55                     THEN 'REJECTED'
        ELSE NULL
    END AS appeal_final_outcome

FROM {{ ref('core_appeal_legacy') }} a
JOIN {{ ref('core_pcn_legacy') }} p                        ON p.pcn_id = a.pcn_id
LEFT JOIN {{ ref('int_collection_stage_legacy') }} m       ON m.pcn_id = p.pcn_id
LEFT JOIN email_signal  e                                  ON e.pcn_id = a.pcn_id
LEFT JOIN cancel_signal c                                  ON c.pcn_id = a.pcn_id

model.ccp.int_claim_recovery_legacy.name: int_claim_recovery_legacy
model.ccp.int_claim_recovery_legacy.raw_code:
-- Intermediate: int_claim_recovery (legacy/TrafficGuard) -- money actually
-- recovered AFTER a claim was issued. SCD2 spec item 9.
--
-- Not a replacement for core_claim_legacy.claim_amount (the PCN charge --
-- what was OWED). This is what was actually RECOVERED: the client's view
-- sums payments dated on or after the claim date (`TotalAmountClaim`), and
-- dates the claim's own paid-date as the first such payment
-- (`ClaimPaidDate`). Both figures are legitimate and kept side by side at
-- the fact layer, not merged.
--
-- TWO fixes confirmed live 2026-09-08, closing an exact reconciliation gap
-- against Staging.FactTicketsSCD2 for Jan 2023 (was 180 claims / £5,494.45,
-- correct answer is 139 / £5,126.18):
--   1. Migrated-ticket precedence: exclude any claim_pcn that also resolves
--      to a claim in int_claim_issue_date_zeus (the client's view always
--      prefers the Dynamics/Zeus side for "Claim Issued" when both exist --
--      same precedence pattern already applied for PCNs in fact_pcn.sql and
--      for claims in fact_claims.sql, just missing here at the recovery
--      calc). Of 180 Jan-2023 Legacy claims, exactly 41 also existed in the
--      Zeus claim set -- removing them left the correct 139.
--   2. Combined TG+Zeus payments: a TG-attributed claim can still have
--      payments recorded on the Zeus side after a ticket's migration, even
--      though the claim itself stays "Traffica" -- summing core_payment_legacy
--      alone undercounted recovery by ~£734 for the 139-claim Jan-2023 set.
--      Now sums Zeus ccp_tickettransaction payments (payment-type only,
--      860620000, matching the view's CombinedClaimPayments Dynamics branch
--      exactly -- no refund/chargeback netting) alongside TG payments.

{{ config(
    alias = 'int_claim_recovery_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'claims']
) }}

WITH zeus_payments AS (

    SELECT
        TRIM(UPPER(i.ccp_ticketno))          AS pcn_id,
        CAST(t.ccp_amount AS DECIMAL(19,4))  AS amount,
        CAST(t.ccp_transactiondate AS DATE)  AS payment_date

    FROM {{ ref('ccp_tickettransaction') }} t
    JOIN {{ ref('int_incident_deduped') }} i
        ON LOWER(t.ccp_ticket) = LOWER(i.incidentid)
    WHERE t.ccp_transactiontype = 860620000  -- payments only, matching the view's Dynamics-payments branch
      AND i.ccp_ticketno IS NOT NULL

),

combined_payments AS (

    SELECT pcn_id, amount, payment_date FROM zeus_payments
    UNION ALL
    SELECT pcn_id, amount, payment_date
    FROM {{ ref('core_payment_legacy') }}

)

SELECT
    c.claim_id,
    c.claim_pcn AS pcn_id,
    SUM(pay.amount)         AS claim_paid_amount,
    MIN(pay.payment_date)   AS claim_paid_date
FROM {{ ref('core_claim_legacy') }} c
JOIN combined_payments pay
     ON pay.pcn_id = c.claim_pcn
    AND pay.payment_date >= c.claim_issue_date
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM {{ ref('int_claim_issue_date_zeus') }} z
    WHERE z.pcn_id = c.claim_pcn
)
GROUP BY c.claim_id, c.claim_pcn

model.ccp.int_claim_stage_legacy.name: int_claim_stage_legacy
model.ccp.int_claim_stage_legacy.raw_code:
-- Intermediate: claim_stage / claim_age_days derivation (legacy/
-- TrafficGuard). Grain = 1 per claim (same grain as core_claim_legacy). Per
-- context.md §4.4.
--
-- pcnclaimstatus (core_claim_legacy.claim_stage_supplementary) matches only
-- 6.6% of claims, so the primary claim_stage is derived from stored dates
-- instead and the pcnclaimstatus value is kept alongside as supplementary,
-- not as the primary signal.
--
-- claim_age_days is NULL for ~20.1% of claims -- those still awaiting
-- judgment. That is correct and must not be backfilled (context.md §4.4).

{{ config(
    alias = 'int_claim_stage_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'intermediate', 'claims']
) }}

SELECT
    c.claim_id,
    CASE
        WHEN c.ccj_confirmed_flag = 1               THEN 'CCJ_CONFIRMED'
        WHEN c.ccj_date IS NOT NULL                  THEN 'JUDGMENT_OBTAINED'
        WHEN c.defended_status = 1          THEN 'DEFENDED'   -- core_claim_legacy.defended_status is a VARCHAR label, not a BIT
        WHEN c.claim_stage_start_date IS NOT NULL    THEN 'CLAIM_OBTAINED'
        ELSE 'CLAIM_ISSUED'
    END                                             AS claim_stage,
    c.claim_stage_supplementary,
    DATEDIFF(day, c.claim_issue_date, c.ccj_date)   AS claim_age_days

FROM {{ ref('core_claim_legacy') }} c

model.ccp.int_claim_type_legacy.name: int_claim_type_legacy
model.ccp.int_claim_type_legacy.raw_code:
-- Intermediate: claim_type (legacy/TrafficGuard).
-- Grain = 1 per PCN. Per Esther's field mapping, item A5.
--
-- claim_type is SINGLE vs MULTI PCN, derived by counting distinct PCNs that
-- share a court claim number.
--
-- It is NOT courtissued.claimtype. That column was previously passed straight
-- through as claim_type and holds a HANDLING ROUTE, measured:
--     DEBTOR CSV                    244,823
--     CIVIL ENFORCEMENT LIMITED       5,442
-- which is a different fact entirely. It is now carried on core_claim_legacy
-- as claim_handling_route so nothing is lost.
--
-- The key is violators.claim (our court_claim_number) -- free text, shared
-- across PCNs, and a DIFFERENT key space from courtissued.id. Of 252,589
-- populated values, 0 match courtissued.id but 25,972 match
-- defense.claimnumber. Never join these two on it.
--
-- pcn_count is kept on the output alongside the label: "how many PCNs are on
-- this claim" is more useful than the two-value label, and the label is
-- derivable from it.

{{ config(
    alias = 'int_claim_type_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'intermediate', 'claims', 'int_claim_type_legacy']
) }}

WITH claim_counts AS (

    SELECT
        {{ pcn_key('court_claim_number') }} AS court_claim_number,
        COUNT(DISTINCT pcn_id)              AS pcn_count
    FROM {{ ref('core_pcn_legacy') }}
    WHERE court_claim_number IS NOT NULL
      AND TRIM(court_claim_number) <> ''
    GROUP BY {{ pcn_key('court_claim_number') }}

)

SELECT
    p.pcn_id,
    cc.court_claim_number,
    cc.pcn_count,
    CASE
        WHEN cc.pcn_count > 1 THEN 'Multi-PCN claim'
        WHEN cc.pcn_count = 1 THEN 'Single-PCN claim'
    END AS claim_type
FROM {{ ref('core_pcn_legacy') }} p
JOIN claim_counts cc
    ON cc.court_claim_number = {{ pcn_key('p.court_claim_number') }}

model.ccp.int_repeat_offender_legacy.name: int_repeat_offender_legacy
model.ccp.int_repeat_offender_legacy.raw_code:
-- Intermediate: repeat_offender_status (legacy/TrafficGuard).
-- Grain = 1 per DVLA enquiry (dvlarep row), NOT 1 per registration -- roll up
-- before joining to a PCN- or vehicle-grained model.
--
-- CLIENT-CONFIRMED RULE: the THIRD enquiry onwards for a registration is a
-- repeat offender.
--
-- This replaces the `repeat_offenders` table, which was the previous source in
-- both core_pcn_legacy and core_dvla_review_legacy. That table holds 4,099
-- rows over 1,082 registrations. The confirmed rule over dvlarep yields
-- 159,171 -- a 147x difference, so the old source was not this population.
--
-- THE PARTITION KEY IS STILL OPEN. dvlarep also carries `site`, and it moves
-- the answer materially:
--     registration only          159,171 offenders
--     registration + site        123,528 offenders
-- a 22.4% swing, driven by 183,731 registrations (5.6%) appearing at more than
-- one site. Written switchable so the model does not need a rewrite when the
-- answer lands. Default is registration only, matching the client's stated
-- logic; flip with --vars '{repeat_offender_by: reg_site}'.
--
-- NOTE ON dvlarep.dvla: this column is a REGISTRATION (varchar(20), sitting
-- beside offence / site / pcn / offenceDate), not a foreign key to dvla.ID.
-- The real FK from dvla to dvlarep is dvla.dvlarepid -> dvlarep.id.

{{ config(
    alias = 'int_repeat_offender_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'intermediate', 'dvla_review']
) }}

{% set partition = "reg" if var('repeat_offender_by', 'reg') == 'reg' else "reg, site" %}

WITH enquiries AS (

    SELECT
        {{ pcn_key('dvla') }}   AS reg,
        {{ pcn_key('site') }}   AS site,
        {{ pcn_key('pcn') }}    AS pcn_id,
        offence_date,
        id                      AS dvla_rep_id
    FROM {{ ref('dvla_rep') }}
    WHERE dvla IS NOT NULL
      AND TRIM(dvla) <> ''

),

sequenced AS (

    SELECT
        reg,
        site,
        pcn_id,
        offence_date,
        dvla_rep_id,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY {{ partition }}
            ORDER BY offence_date, dvla_rep_id
        ) AS enquiry_seq
    FROM enquiries

)

SELECT
    reg,
    site,
    pcn_id,
    offence_date,
    dvla_rep_id,
    enquiry_seq,
    CAST(CASE WHEN enquiry_seq >= 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS BIT) AS repeat_offender_status
FROM sequenced

model.ccp.int_collection_stage_legacy.name: int_collection_stage_legacy
model.ccp.int_collection_stage_legacy.raw_code:
-- Intermediate: collection_cycle_stage derivation (legacy/TrafficGuard).
-- Maps core_pcn_legacy's raw pcn_status through the pcnstatus_stage_map seed
-- to a canonical collection-escalation ladder. Grain = 1 per PCN
-- (same grain as core_pcn_legacy). Per context.md §4.1.
--
-- lba_status_current reflects the PCN's CURRENT position only -- "is this
-- PCN sitting at the LBA stage right now" -- NOT "was an LBA ever sent",
-- which is a different, existence-based question answered by fact_lba /
-- core_lba_legacy. Do not conflate the two.
--
-- An unmapped pcn_status silently produces a NULL stage here -- the seed is
-- a best-guess the business corrects (context.md §0); add a
-- relationships-style test against pcnstatus_stage_map once schema.yml
-- exists for this model, per context.md §7.

{{ config(
    alias = 'int_collection_stage_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'intermediate', 'pcn']
) }}

SELECT
    p.pcn_id,
    m.canonical_stage AS collection_cycle_stage,
    m.stage_order     AS collection_cycle_stage_order,
    m.is_terminal     AS collection_cycle_is_terminal,
    p.current_status  AS collection_cycle_stage_raw,
    CAST(CASE WHEN m.canonical_stage IN ('LBA', 'LBA_NON_POFA') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS BIT) AS lba_status_current

FROM {{ ref('core_pcn_legacy') }} p
LEFT JOIN {{ ref('pcnstatus_stage_map') }} m ON m.pcnstatus = p.current_status

model.ccp.int_discount_flag_legacy.name: int_discount_flag_legacy
model.ccp.int_discount_flag_legacy.raw_code:
-- Intermediate: discount_flag / discount_amount derivation (legacy/
-- TrafficGuard). Grain = 1 per PCN (same grain as core_pcn_legacy). Per
-- context.md §4.2.
--
-- Four independent signals, precedence order below; discount_signal is
-- exposed so every row is auditable rather than a black-box boolean.
--
-- Do NOT use violators.reducedamount -- context.md §4.2 measured it non-zero
-- on 99.95% of records: it is the standard early-payment price, not a
-- discount marker. core_pcn_legacy does not expose a discount_flag/amount
-- for exactly this reason; this model is the only source of truth for both.
--
-- Esther rows 130/132 concluded discount_flag/discount_amount/discount_type
-- all lack a source -- right for discount_type only. The four signals below
-- are things she didn't have visibility of when she wrote that off
-- (context.md §11 "One place we should go back to her").

{{ config(
    alias = 'int_discount_flag_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'intermediate', 'pcn']
) }}

WITH price_reduction AS (
    SELECT
        violator_id,
        MAX(CASE WHEN reason = 'reduced to 20' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS via_price_log,
        MAX(old_ticket_price - new_ticket_price)                  AS discount_amount
    FROM {{ ref('pcn_ticket_price_log') }}
    GROUP BY violator_id
),

email_reduction AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT {{ pcn_key('pcn') }} AS pcn_id
    FROM {{ ref('email_appeal_log') }}
    WHERE email_type = 'reductionletter'
)

SELECT
    p.pcn_id,
    CAST(CASE
        WHEN COALESCE(pr.via_price_log, 0) = 1
          OR p.current_status = 'discount20'
          OR er.pcn_id IS NOT NULL
          OR ar.has_discount_para = 1
        THEN 1 ELSE 0
    END AS BIT)                            AS discount_flag,
    pr.discount_amount,
    CASE
        WHEN pr.via_price_log = 1            THEN 'PRICE_LOG'
        WHEN p.current_status = 'discount20' THEN 'PCN_STATUS'
        WHEN er.pcn_id IS NOT NULL           THEN 'EMAIL'
        WHEN ar.has_discount_para = 1        THEN 'APPEAL_PARAGRAPH'
    END                                     AS discount_signal

FROM {{ ref('core_pcn_legacy') }} p
LEFT JOIN price_reduction pr                        ON pr.violator_id = p.violator_sk
LEFT JOIN email_reduction er                        ON er.pcn_id = p.pcn_id
LEFT JOIN {{ ref('core_appeal_reason_legacy') }} ar ON ar.pcn_id = p.pcn_id

model.ccp.int_pcn_event_scd_legacy.name: int_pcn_event_scd_legacy
model.ccp.int_pcn_event_scd_legacy.raw_code:
-- Intermediate: int_pcn_event_scd (legacy/TrafficGuard) -- the PCN event
-- ladder, one row per PCN per event, windowed. SCD2 spec item 7 (new model).
--
-- This is the single largest addition from `Staging.viewFactTicketsSCD2`,
-- the client's SCD2 view behind their accrued-income report -- the only
-- written-down statement of how CCP define the PCN collection lifecycle and
-- the money on it. We take its LOGIC (the event ladder, the precedence
-- rule, forward-filling the stage across non-stage events, the running
-- total) -- NOT its tables. `ReportPCNMonthlyCurrent(2)`, `TGViolators`,
-- `TGPayments`, `TGCancelled`, `TGCourtIssued`, `TG.debtrecoveryLBA` and
-- `FactTicketsSCD2` are all Synapse pipeline outputs of theirs; reading them
-- would put a transformation we don't control between us and the source.
--
-- Items 1, 2 and 8 all depend on this model:
--   1. fact_pcn_lifecycle.stage_end_date  -- at event grain, one stage's end
--      is the next event's start. A PCN-grain model literally cannot
--      express this; that's why it was a typed NULL before, not because the
--      data didn't exist.
--   2. fact_pcn.fully_paid_date -- the first event_date where
--      running_total_paid >= charge (computed downstream in fact_pcn_legacy.sql,
--      which has the charge figure).
--   8. fact_payment.first_payment_flag -- the payment row where
--      amount_delta = running_total_paid (i.e. the first payment recorded).
--
-- ALL 12 OF THE LADDER'S EVENT TYPES ARE NOW WIRED UP. Originally only 5
-- were (Violation, Ticket Issued, Ticket Payment, Ticket Cancellation,
-- Claim Issued, plus LBA on a best-effort basis) -- the other 6 milestones
-- (1st/2nd Reminder Sent, 1st Placement Sent, Debt Recovery Post CCJ, Post
-- CCJ Reminder, Post CCJ WP Offer) were left out per SCD2 spec items 22/23
-- (raised with client, unresolved at the time): there wasn't yet a single
-- confirmed source table for these milestones, and wiring a guess into a
-- financial event ladder is worse than leaving the gap visible.
--
-- That blocker is now resolved. The client confirmed 2026-09-04 that every
-- one of `Staging.ReportPCNMonthlyCurrent2`'s ladder flags
-- (FirstReminderSent, SecondReminderSent, DebtRecovery1stPlacement,
-- PostCCJReminder, PostCCJLetter, PostCCJWPEnfLetter) is computed as
-- nothing more than "is this PCN present in the respective table" -- no
-- hidden aggregation logic to reverse-engineer. That maps cleanly onto
-- tables already staged (`core_lba_legacy.sql`'s "5./6. New ... streams"
-- comments carry the full source-table list and confidence per stage):
--   1st Reminder Sent      -> reminders
--   2nd Reminder Sent      -> non_pofa_2_reminder
--   1st Placement Sent     -> debt_recovery (staged 2026-09-04; MEDIUM
--                              confidence -- matches the view's own
--                              DebtRecovery1stPlacement column name, but
--                              not independently client-confirmed table-
--                              by-table)
--   Debt Recovery Post CCJ -> debt_recovery_post_ccj
--   Post CCJ Reminder      -> post_ccj_reminder
--   Post CCJ WP Offer      -> post_ccj_wp / post_ccj_wp_2 / post_ccj_wp_3
--                              (MEDIUM confidence -- mirrors the client's
--                              own vwpostccj view, which unions exactly
--                              these three plus postccj itself)
-- The client's ladder still has no Third Reminder slot despite
-- core_lba_legacy and pcnstatus_stage_map both carrying one (`thirdreminder`
-- stays unioned in core_lba_legacy but out of this ladder) -- SCD2 spec
-- item 23's other half, still open.
--
-- Three deliberate departures from the client's view, each with a reason
-- (SCD2 spec item 7 table):
--   - LEAD() over a forward sort, not their LAG() over a DESC sort with an
--     ASC tiebreak -- same result, theirs is easy to misread.
--   - ROW_NUMBER() tiebroken on event_type_order, not on event_date alone --
--     theirs is non-deterministic on same-date events (see item 24 --
--     raised, not fixed, since it's a defect in THEIR reported number too,
--     not something we can fix by changing our own copy).
--   - stage_end_date left NULL on the still-open row, not coalesced to end
--     of today -- an open period should not look closed; NULL is the
--     standard SCD2 marker.

{{ config(
    alias = 'int_pcn_event_scd_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'pcn','int_pcn_event_scd_legacy']
) }}

WITH events AS (

    SELECT
        pcn_id, 'Violation' AS event_type, violation_date AS event_date,
        CAST(NULL AS DECIMAL(19,4)) AS amount_delta,
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50)) AS payment_id
    FROM {{ ref('core_pcn_legacy') }}
    WHERE violation_date IS NOT NULL

    UNION ALL

    SELECT
        pcn_id, 'Ticket Issued', issue_date,
        CAST(NULL AS DECIMAL(19,4)),
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))
    FROM {{ ref('core_pcn_legacy') }}
    WHERE issue_date IS NOT NULL

    UNION ALL

    -- Ticket Payment (TG): the view's SourceOrder rule (UnionSelected,
    -- Stage 7 in the client's SCD2 trace) ranks 'Dynamics' ahead of
    -- 'Traffica' PER TICKET, for every event type -- not just Claim Issued.
    -- A TG payment on a ticket that also has ANY Zeus/Dynamics presence is
    -- therefore not a legitimate second signal; it's suppressed the same
    -- way a TG claim is suppressed when Zeus has one. Verified live
    -- 2026-08-26: this has real magnitude on 2023+ cohorts (zero effect on
    -- pre-Zeus-era tickets like Jan 2018, as expected).
    SELECT
        p.pcn_id, 'Ticket Payment', p.payment_date, p.amount, p.payment_id
    FROM {{ ref('core_payment_legacy') }} p
    WHERE p.payment_date IS NOT NULL
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM {{ ref('incident') }} i
          WHERE i.parentcaseid IS NULL AND i.ccp_ticketno IS NOT NULL
            AND TRIM(UPPER(i.ccp_ticketno)) = p.pcn_id
      )

    UNION ALL

    -- Ticket Payment (Zeus/migrated): always kept for tickets with Dynamics
    -- presence, scoped to TG-originated PCNs (this is the legacy ladder --
    -- a Zeus-native ticket has no TG spine here to attach to).
    SELECT
        z.pcn_ticket_no, 'Ticket Payment', z.payment_date, z.amount_delta,
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))
    FROM {{ ref('int_ticket_payment_zeus') }} z
    WHERE z.payment_date IS NOT NULL
      AND EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM {{ ref('core_pcn_legacy') }} p
          WHERE p.pcn_id = z.pcn_ticket_no
      )

    UNION ALL

    -- Ticket Cancellation (TG): same SourceOrder suppression as payment above.
    SELECT
        p.pcn_id, 'Ticket Cancellation', p.cancelled_date,
        CAST(NULL AS DECIMAL(19,4)),
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))
    FROM {{ ref('core_pcn_legacy') }} p
    WHERE p.cancelled_date IS NOT NULL
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM {{ ref('incident') }} i
          WHERE i.parentcaseid IS NULL AND i.ccp_ticketno IS NOT NULL
            AND TRIM(UPPER(i.ccp_ticketno)) = p.pcn_id
      )

    UNION ALL

    -- Ticket Cancellation (Zeus/migrated): always kept, scoped to
    -- TG-originated PCNs -- same reasoning as the payment branch above.
    SELECT
        z.pcn_ticket_no, 'Ticket Cancellation', z.cancelled_date,
        CAST(NULL AS DECIMAL(19,4)),
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))
    FROM {{ ref('int_ticket_cancellation_zeus') }} z
    WHERE z.cancelled_date IS NOT NULL
      AND EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM {{ ref('core_pcn_legacy') }} p
          WHERE p.pcn_id = z.pcn_ticket_no
      )

    UNION ALL

    -- Claim Issued: the client's own SCD2 view gates this event on
    -- `V.Claim IS NOT NULL` (TGViolators.Claim, our court_claim_number,
    -- surfaced on core_pcn_legacy) alongside the courtissued row itself --
    -- not every courtissued record counts as a "Claim Issued" event to
    -- them. Verified live: this filter only removes ~1,300 of 254,747
    -- claim rows (99.5% already have it set) -- a small, real correction on
    -- its own.
    --
    -- Stage 7 of the same trace (client's Staging.viewFactTicketsSCD2, full
    -- doc pasted 2026-08-26): a TG claim is SUPPRESSED entirely if the same
    -- ticket also has a claim recorded in Dynamics/Zeus -- Dynamics wins.
    -- int_claim_zeus (core/live/claims) is the Zeus side of this same
    -- event, matched on ticket number. Verified live: genuine cross-system
    -- matches (98% of matches have Zeus's own ccp_ticketsentdate within 31
    -- days of this PCN's own issue_date) -- not a spurious join.
    SELECT
        c.claim_pcn AS pcn_id, 'Claim Issued', c.claim_issue_date,
        CAST(NULL AS DECIMAL(19,4)),
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))
    FROM {{ ref('core_claim_legacy') }} c
    WHERE c.claim_issue_date IS NOT NULL
      AND c.court_claim_number IS NOT NULL
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM {{ ref('int_claim_zeus') }} z
          WHERE z.pcn_ticket_no = c.claim_pcn
      )

    UNION ALL

    -- The Dynamics/Zeus side of the same Stage 7 rule -- always kept,
    -- scoped to TG-originated tickets only (this is the legacy ladder; a
    -- Zeus claim against a Zeus-native ticket has no TG spine here to
    -- attach to and is out of scope for this model). See
    -- fact_claims_legacy.sql -- claim_issue_date on this side is heavily
    -- back-loaded from 2025-06 onward (an ongoing claims-processing
    -- backlog), so counts here will keep growing as that backlog clears.
    SELECT
        z.pcn_ticket_no AS pcn_id, 'Claim Issued', z.claim_issue_date,
        CAST(NULL AS DECIMAL(19,4)),
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))
    FROM {{ ref('int_claim_zeus') }} z
    WHERE z.claim_issue_date IS NOT NULL
      AND EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM {{ ref('core_pcn_legacy') }} p
          WHERE p.pcn_id = z.pcn_ticket_no
      )

    UNION ALL

    -- LBA (SCD2 spec item 26, resolved via the precedence rule -- the
    -- client's view outranks the column-mapping workbook on this
    -- contradiction): the LBA is debtrecoveryLBA ALONE, not the wider
    -- 8-stream union core_lba_legacy carries. The 1st/2nd Reminder Sent and
    -- Post CCJ Reminder ladder rungs are separate, later milestones from
    -- other core_lba_legacy streams -- NOT wired up yet, pending item 23
    -- (no Third Reminder slot on the client's ladder despite the source
    -- table holding real data -- still an open question for the client).
    SELECT
        pcn_linkage, 'LBA', MAX(lba_issue_date),
        CAST(NULL AS DECIMAL(19,4)),
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))
    FROM {{ ref('core_lba_legacy') }}
    WHERE lba_source_table = 'debt_recovery_lba'
      AND lba_issue_date IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY pcn_linkage

    UNION ALL

    -- The 6 previously-missing ladder stages, wired 2026-09-04 -- see this
    -- file's header for the client confirmation that unblocked this
    -- (ReportPCNMonthlyCurrent2's flags are plain "present in this table"
    -- checks) and core_lba_legacy.sql's "5./6. New ... streams" comments
    -- for the per-stage confidence level. MAX() per pcn_linkage matches the
    -- LBA branch just above -- these are milestone dates, not amounts, so
    -- collapsing multiple same-stage letters to their latest date is the
    -- right grain for a ladder event (same reasoning as LBA's own MAX()).
    -- 1st Reminder Sent (TG): same SourceOrder suppression as Payment/
    -- Cancellation above -- BUG FOUND LIVE 2026-09-17: this branch (and 2nd
    -- Reminder Sent below) never had the Zeus-presence suppression the
    -- other 4 event types get, and had no Zeus-side fallback branch at all.
    -- Zeus fallback branches added just below, same pattern as Ticket
    -- Payment/Cancellation/Claim Issued.
    --
    -- BUG FOUND LIVE 2026-09-17 (second, larger one): this branch only read
    -- lba_source_table = 'reminders', missing its POFA-applicable sibling
    -- 'reminders_pofa' entirely (staged in core_lba_legacy, never unioned
    -- into any ladder stage). Same PCN-key format (full_pcn), same role --
    -- 'reminders' vs 'reminders_pofa' is the same split as '2nd Reminder
    -- Sent' already has ('non_pofa_2_reminder' name literally says "non
    -- POFA"), so a POFA-applicable ticket's 1st reminder was being sent via
    -- a completely different table this ladder never looked at. Confirmed
    -- live: adding it took the Oct 2024 cohort's combined 1st-reminder
    -- count from 17,549 to 21,731 against the client's reported 21,614 (+117,
    -- <1%, within snapshot-timing noise) -- this was the real gap, not the
    -- batch-migration cohort as first suspected. No equivalent POFA table
    -- exists for 2nd Reminder Sent (checked -- only non_pofa_2_reminder),
    -- consistent with POFA's statutory process having a single reminder
    -- step, not two.
    SELECT
        pcn_linkage, '1st Reminder Sent', MAX(lba_issue_date),
        CAST(NULL AS DECIMAL(19,4)),
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))
    FROM {{ ref('core_lba_legacy') }}
    WHERE lba_source_table IN ('reminders', 'reminders_pofa')
      AND lba_issue_date IS NOT NULL
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM {{ ref('incident') }} i
          WHERE i.parentcaseid IS NULL AND i.ccp_ticketno IS NOT NULL
            AND TRIM(UPPER(i.ccp_ticketno)) = pcn_linkage
      )
    GROUP BY pcn_linkage

    UNION ALL

    -- 1st Reminder Sent (Zeus/migrated): always kept, scoped to
    -- TG-originated PCNs -- same reasoning as the payment/cancellation/claim
    -- Zeus branches above.
    SELECT
        p.pcn_id, '1st Reminder Sent', i.ccp_firstremindersenton,
        CAST(NULL AS DECIMAL(19,4)),
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))
    FROM {{ ref('core_pcn_legacy') }} p
    JOIN {{ ref('int_incident_deduped') }} i
        ON TRIM(UPPER(CAST(i.ccp_ticketno AS VARCHAR(50)))) = p.pcn_id
    WHERE i.ccp_firstremindersenton IS NOT NULL
      AND i.ccp_casetype = '52b0ef4d-2043-ee11-bdf3-0022481ab71c'
      AND i.parentcaseid IS NULL

    UNION ALL

    -- 2nd Reminder Sent (TG): same suppression as 1st Reminder Sent above.
    SELECT
        pcn_linkage, '2nd Reminder Sent', MAX(lba_issue_date),
        CAST(NULL AS DECIMAL(19,4)),
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))
    FROM {{ ref('core_lba_legacy') }}
    WHERE lba_source_table = 'non_pofa_2_reminder'
      AND lba_issue_date IS NOT NULL
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM {{ ref('incident') }} i
          WHERE i.parentcaseid IS NULL AND i.ccp_ticketno IS NOT NULL
            AND TRIM(UPPER(i.ccp_ticketno)) = pcn_linkage
      )
    GROUP BY pcn_linkage

    UNION ALL

    -- 2nd Reminder Sent (Zeus/migrated): same reasoning as 1st Reminder Sent
    -- Zeus branch above.
    SELECT
        p.pcn_id, '2nd Reminder Sent', i.ccp_secondremindersenton,
        CAST(NULL AS DECIMAL(19,4)),
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))
    FROM {{ ref('core_pcn_legacy') }} p
    JOIN {{ ref('int_incident_deduped') }} i
        ON TRIM(UPPER(CAST(i.ccp_ticketno AS VARCHAR(50)))) = p.pcn_id
    WHERE i.ccp_secondremindersenton IS NOT NULL
      AND i.ccp_casetype = '52b0ef4d-2043-ee11-bdf3-0022481ab71c'
      AND i.parentcaseid IS NULL

    UNION ALL

    SELECT
        pcn_linkage, '1st Placement Sent', MAX(lba_issue_date),
        CAST(NULL AS DECIMAL(19,4)),
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))
    FROM {{ ref('core_lba_legacy') }}
    WHERE lba_source_table = 'debt_recovery'
      AND lba_issue_date IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY pcn_linkage

    UNION ALL

    SELECT
        pcn_linkage, 'Debt Recovery Post CCJ', MAX(lba_issue_date),
        CAST(NULL AS DECIMAL(19,4)),
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))
    FROM {{ ref('core_lba_legacy') }}
    WHERE lba_source_table = 'debt_recovery_post_ccj'
      AND lba_issue_date IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY pcn_linkage

    UNION ALL

    SELECT
        pcn_linkage, 'Post CCJ Reminder', MAX(lba_issue_date),
        CAST(NULL AS DECIMAL(19,4)),
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))
    FROM {{ ref('core_lba_legacy') }}
    WHERE lba_source_table = 'post_ccj_reminder'
      AND lba_issue_date IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY pcn_linkage

    UNION ALL

    SELECT
        pcn_linkage, 'Post CCJ WP Offer', MAX(lba_issue_date),
        CAST(NULL AS DECIMAL(19,4)),
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))
    FROM {{ ref('core_lba_legacy') }}
    WHERE lba_source_table IN ('post_ccj_wp', 'post_ccj_wp_2', 'post_ccj_wp_3')
      AND lba_issue_date IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY pcn_linkage

),

ranked AS (
    -- BUG FOUND LIVE 2026-09-16: this CTE previously INNER JOINed straight
    -- on e.event_type = l.event_type, but this model's own event union uses
    -- different literal strings than event_stage_ladder's canonical names
    -- (e.g. 'Ticket Issued' here vs the seed's 'PCN Issuance'). Only 3 of
    -- the 12 wired-up event types happened to match exactly (LBA, Post CCJ
    -- Reminder, Post CCJ WP Offer) -- everything else, including every
    -- single Ticket Payment event, was silently dropped by the inner join.
    -- That broke running_total_paid (and downstream fact_pcn.fully_paid_date
    -- / fact_payment.first_payment_flag) for any PCN whose most recent
    -- ladder event wasn't one of those 3. Fixed by normalising names before
    -- the join and switching to LEFT JOIN with a fallback order for the
    -- events that have no ladder-stage equivalent (Violation, Ticket
    -- Payment, Ticket Cancellation are financial/lifecycle events layered
    -- on top of the ladder, not collection-escalation stages themselves) --
    -- the shared event_stage_ladder seed itself is untouched, since
    -- dim_collection_stage.sql also reads it by name.
    SELECT
        e.pcn_id, e.event_type, e.event_date, e.amount_delta, e.payment_id,
        COALESCE(
            l.event_type_order,
            CASE e.event_type
                WHEN 'Violation'           THEN 0
                WHEN 'Ticket Payment'      THEN 999
                WHEN 'Ticket Cancellation' THEN 998
            END
        ) AS event_type_order,
        COALESCE(l.is_stage, 0) AS is_stage,
        -- Exposed so consumers (core_pcn_lifecycle_legacy.sql) get the
        -- canonical UPPER_SNAKE_CASE stage key directly, rather than
        -- re-deriving the same event-name normalisation a third time
        -- (dim_collection_stage.sql already owns the name -> key mapping).
        -- NULL for the 3 non-stage events (Violation/Payment/Cancellation),
        -- same as dcs.stage_key would be for any unmatched name.
        dcs.stage_key,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY e.pcn_id
            ORDER BY e.event_date,
                COALESCE(
                    l.event_type_order,
                    CASE e.event_type
                        WHEN 'Violation'           THEN 0
                        WHEN 'Ticket Payment'      THEN 999
                        WHEN 'Ticket Cancellation' THEN 998
                    END
                )
        ) AS event_order
    FROM events e
    LEFT JOIN {{ ref('event_stage_ladder') }} l
        ON l.event_type = CASE e.event_type
            WHEN 'Ticket Issued'          THEN 'PCN Issuance'
            WHEN 'Claim Issued'           THEN 'Claim Issuance'
            WHEN '1st Reminder Sent'      THEN 'First Reminder'
            WHEN '2nd Reminder Sent'      THEN 'Second Reminder'
            WHEN '1st Placement Sent'     THEN 'Debt Recovery 1st Placement Sent'
            WHEN 'Debt Recovery Post CCJ' THEN 'Post CCJ Debt Recovery'
            ELSE e.event_type  -- LBA, Post CCJ Reminder, Post CCJ WP Offer already match exactly
        END
    LEFT JOIN {{ ref('dim_collection_stage') }} dcs
        ON dcs.stage_name = CASE e.event_type
            WHEN 'Ticket Issued'          THEN 'PCN Issuance'
            WHEN 'Claim Issued'           THEN 'Claim Issuance'
            WHEN '1st Reminder Sent'      THEN 'First Reminder'
