            WHEN '2nd Reminder Sent'      THEN 'Second Reminder'
            WHEN '1st Placement Sent'     THEN 'Debt Recovery 1st Placement Sent'
            WHEN 'Debt Recovery Post CCJ' THEN 'Post CCJ Debt Recovery'
            ELSE e.event_type
        END
    WHERE e.event_date IS NOT NULL
),

windowed AS (
    SELECT
        r.*,
        -- BUG FOUND LIVE: MAX(event_type) on the raw string picks the
        -- ALPHABETICALLY highest stage name, not the most recent one --
        -- confirmed live, every LBA-then-later-Ticket-Issued sequence
        -- wrongly reported 'Ticket Issued' as filled_stage at the LBA
        -- event's own row, since 'T' > 'L'. Encoding event_order into the
        -- string before taking MAX(), then stripping it back off, makes the
        -- comparison numeric-order-correct instead of alphabetical.
        SUBSTRING(
            MAX(CASE WHEN r.is_stage = 1
                     THEN RIGHT('0000000000' + CAST(r.event_order AS VARCHAR(10)), 10) + '|' + r.event_type
                     END) OVER (
                PARTITION BY r.pcn_id ORDER BY r.event_order
                ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING
            ),
            12, 100
        ) AS filled_stage,
        SUM(r.amount_delta) OVER (
            PARTITION BY r.pcn_id ORDER BY r.event_order
            ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING
        ) AS running_total_paid,
        LEAD(r.event_date) OVER (
            PARTITION BY r.pcn_id ORDER BY r.event_order
        ) AS next_event_date
    FROM ranked r
)

SELECT
    pcn_id, event_type, stage_key, event_type_order, event_order, filled_stage,
    event_date                                          AS stage_start_date,
    DATEADD(millisecond, -1, next_event_date)           AS stage_end_date,   -- NULL on the still-open row -- see header
    amount_delta                                        AS amount_paid,
    running_total_paid,
    payment_id,
    CAST(CASE WHEN amount_delta IS NOT NULL
               AND amount_delta = running_total_paid
              THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS BIT)                 AS first_payment_flag
FROM windowed

model.ccp.core_lba_legacy.name: core_lba_legacy
model.ccp.core_lba_legacy.raw_code:
-- Core legacy LBA events (Built from Traffic Gaurd), one row per LBA/reminder letter sent.
-- Unions the LBAReminder-family letters (LBAReminder = PRIMARY per context.md's
-- updated §5.1/§7.9 -- the other 4 are companion reminders: NonPofa2reminder,
-- Thirdreminder, PostCCJReminder, PostCCJ14daysReminder) enriched with
-- lettertemplates/lettertypes for lba_type/lba_template, plus the companion
-- streams Reminders, Reminderspofa, and debtrecoveryLBA.
-- NTK is intentionally excluded here -- per context.md §6.3/§7.9 it belongs to
-- the future core__letter entity as its own tagged stream, not this table, and
-- the source mapping's lba_id anchor set (LBAReminder, Reminders,
-- debtrecoveryLBA) does not include it.
-- Every stream's pcn_linkage is TRIM/UPPER-normalised (context.md §9 rule 1) --
-- some streams key on the full_pcn form, some on the shorter pcn form (§5.1
-- "Two different PCN keys" warning); normalising here means callers never need
-- to know which.
-- Final table grain = 1 per LBA/reminder letter event (lba_id).

{{ config(
    alias = 'core_lba_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'lba']
) }}

WITH

-- 1. Template -> letter type lookup, shared by the LBAReminder-family sources below.
letter_type_lookup AS (
    SELECT
        lt.id               AS template_id,
        lt.template_name    AS lba_template,
        ltyp.type           AS lba_type
    FROM {{ ref('letter_templates') }} lt
    LEFT JOIN {{ ref('letter_types') }} ltyp
        ON ltyp.id = lt.template_letter_type_id
),

-- 2. LBAReminder-family: pcn, date_sent, batch_id, template_id -- resolved via the lookup above.
lba_reminder_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('lba_reminder-', CAST(r.id AS VARCHAR(20)))    AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(r.pcn))                                    AS pcn_linkage,
        COALESCE(lkp.lba_type, 'LBA Reminder')                AS lba_type,
        lkp.lba_template                                      AS lba_template,
        r.date_sent                                           AS lba_issue_date,
        r.batch_id                                            AS batch_id,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                     AS written_off,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                     AS solicitors,
        'lba_reminder'                                        AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('lba_reminder') }} r
    LEFT JOIN letter_type_lookup lkp ON lkp.template_id = r.template_id
    WHERE r.pcn IS NOT NULL AND r.pcn <> ''
),

non_pofa_2_reminder_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('non_pofa_2_reminder-', CAST(r.id AS VARCHAR(20))) AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(r.pcn))                                        AS pcn_linkage,
        COALESCE(lkp.lba_type, 'Non-POFA 2nd Reminder')           AS lba_type,
        lkp.lba_template                                          AS lba_template,
        r.date_sent                                               AS lba_issue_date,
        r.batch_id                                                AS batch_id,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                         AS written_off,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                         AS solicitors,
        'non_pofa_2_reminder'                                     AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('non_pofa_2_reminder') }} r
    LEFT JOIN letter_type_lookup lkp ON lkp.template_id = r.template_id
    WHERE r.pcn IS NOT NULL AND r.pcn <> ''
),

third_reminder_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('third_reminder-', CAST(r.id AS VARCHAR(20)))  AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(r.pcn))                                    AS pcn_linkage,
        COALESCE(lkp.lba_type, 'Third Reminder')              AS lba_type,
        lkp.lba_template                                      AS lba_template,
        r.date_sent                                           AS lba_issue_date,
        r.batch_id                                            AS batch_id,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                     AS written_off,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                     AS solicitors,
        'third_reminder'                                      AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('third_reminder') }} r
    LEFT JOIN letter_type_lookup lkp ON lkp.template_id = r.template_id
    WHERE r.pcn IS NOT NULL AND r.pcn <> ''
),

post_ccj_reminder_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('post_ccj_reminder-', CAST(r.id AS VARCHAR(20))) AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(r.pcn))                                      AS pcn_linkage,
        COALESCE(lkp.lba_type, 'Post-CCJ Reminder')             AS lba_type,
        lkp.lba_template                                        AS lba_template,
        r.date_sent                                             AS lba_issue_date,
        r.batch_id                                              AS batch_id,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                       AS written_off,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                       AS solicitors,
        'post_ccj_reminder'                                     AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('post_ccj_reminder') }} r
    LEFT JOIN letter_type_lookup lkp ON lkp.template_id = r.template_id
    WHERE r.pcn IS NOT NULL AND r.pcn <> ''
),

post_ccj_14_days_reminder_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('post_ccj_14_days_reminder-', CAST(r.id AS VARCHAR(20))) AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(r.pcn))                                              AS pcn_linkage,
        COALESCE(lkp.lba_type, 'Post-CCJ 14 Day Reminder')              AS lba_type,
        lkp.lba_template                                                AS lba_template,
        r.date_sent                                                     AS lba_issue_date,
        r.batch_id                                                      AS batch_id,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                               AS written_off,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                               AS solicitors,
        'post_ccj_14_days_reminder'                                     AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('post_ccj_14_days_reminder') }} r
    LEFT JOIN letter_type_lookup lkp ON lkp.template_id = r.template_id
    WHERE r.pcn IS NOT NULL AND r.pcn <> ''
),

-- 3. Reminders / Reminderspofa: no template link, so lba_type is a fixed label.
--    Uses full_pcn (not the shorter pcn column) as the canonical linkage key.
reminders_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('reminders-', CAST(id AS VARCHAR(20)))  AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(full_pcn))                          AS pcn_linkage,
        'Reminder'                                      AS lba_type,
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))                       AS lba_template,
        reminder                                        AS lba_issue_date,
        batch_id                                        AS batch_id,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                               AS written_off,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                               AS solicitors,
        'reminders'                                     AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('reminders') }}
    WHERE full_pcn IS NOT NULL AND full_pcn <> ''
),

reminders_pofa_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('reminders_pofa-', CAST(id AS VARCHAR(20))) AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(full_pcn))                              AS pcn_linkage,
        'Reminder (POFA)'                                  AS lba_type,
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))                          AS lba_template,
        reminder_date                                      AS lba_issue_date,
        batch_id                                           AS batch_id,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                  AS written_off,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                  AS solicitors,
        'reminders_pofa'                                   AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('reminders_pofa') }}
    WHERE full_pcn IS NOT NULL AND full_pcn <> ''
),

-- 4. debtrecoveryLBA: dr_type is NOT usable as a letter type -- context.md §7.9
--    confirms it's a single distinct value across all 4,495 rows ('DRPL',
--    verified empirically too). Fixed label instead, matching the other
--    hardcoded-label streams below.
debt_recovery_lba_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('debt_recovery_lba-', CAST(id AS VARCHAR(20))) AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(pcn))                                      AS pcn_linkage,
        'Debt Recovery / LBA'                                 AS lba_type,
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))                             AS lba_template,
        debt_recovery_date                                    AS lba_issue_date,
        batch_id                                              AS batch_id,
        written_off,
        solicitors,
        'debt_recovery_lba'                                   AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('debt_recovery_lba') }}
    WHERE pcn IS NOT NULL AND pcn <> ''
),

-- 5. New debt-recovery / legal-letter streams, added 2026-09-04 -- surfaced
--    by the client's `getAmountOutstanding`/`reportpcnissued2` stored
--    procedures, which reference dozens of TrafficGuard tables that were
--    already sitting in lh_raw but had never been staged. This model's own
--    original comment marked it as "the eventual home for the 1st/2nd
--    Reminder Sent / Post CCJ Reminder milestones once wired up" (see
--    fact_lba_legacy.sql header) -- these are exactly that: additional
--    debt-recovery/legal letter-event streams, unioned in at the same
--    letter-event grain, each labelled by lba_source_table like every
--    stream above. NONE of these are wired into
--    int_pcn_event_scd_legacy.sql's financial ladder or
--    event_stage_ladder.csv -- that file's header explains why guessing at
--    stage precedence for a financial event ladder is worse than leaving
--    the gap visible, and multiple of these new streams (debtrecovery vs
--    debtrecovery2, drreturned vs drreturned2) are exactly the kind of
--    multi-candidate ambiguity it warns about. They are unioned here, as
--    data, not yet as ladder stages -- the ladder-wiring decision is still
--    open.
debt_recovery_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('debt_recovery-', CAST(id AS VARCHAR(20)))  AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(pcn))                                   AS pcn_linkage,
        'Debt Recovery'                                    AS lba_type,
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))                          AS lba_template,
        debt_recovery_date                                 AS lba_issue_date,
        batch_id                                           AS batch_id,
        written_off,
        solicitors,
        'debt_recovery'                                    AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('debt_recovery') }}
    WHERE pcn IS NOT NULL AND pcn <> ''
),

debt_recovery_2_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('debt_recovery_2-', CAST(id AS VARCHAR(20))) AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(pcn))                                    AS pcn_linkage,
        'Debt Recovery (2)'                                 AS lba_type,
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))                           AS lba_template,
        debtrecoverydate                                    AS lba_issue_date,
        batchid                                             AS batch_id,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                   AS written_off,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                   AS solicitors,
        'debt_recovery_2'                                   AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('debt_recovery_2') }}
    WHERE pcn IS NOT NULL AND pcn <> ''
),

-- dr_returned/dr_returned_2/dr_returned_post_ccj are their own dedicated
-- "debt recovery returned" event logs (id, pcn, dateadded, datereturned) --
-- the milestone is the RETURN itself, so lba_issue_date anchors on
-- datereturned, falling back to dateadded only when a return was logged
-- without its own date.
dr_returned_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('dr_returned-', CAST(id AS VARCHAR(20)))    AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(pcn))                                   AS pcn_linkage,
        'Debt Recovery Returned'                           AS lba_type,
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))                          AS lba_template,
        COALESCE(datereturned, dateadded)                  AS lba_issue_date,
        batchid                                            AS batch_id,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                  AS written_off,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                  AS solicitors,
        'dr_returned'                                       AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('dr_returned') }}
    WHERE pcn IS NOT NULL AND pcn <> ''
),

dr_returned_2_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('dr_returned_2-', CAST(id AS VARCHAR(20)))  AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(pcn))                                   AS pcn_linkage,
        'Debt Recovery Returned (2)'                       AS lba_type,
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))                          AS lba_template,
        COALESCE(datereturned, dateadded)                  AS lba_issue_date,
        batchid                                            AS batch_id,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                  AS written_off,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                  AS solicitors,
        'dr_returned_2'                                     AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('dr_returned_2') }}
    WHERE pcn IS NOT NULL AND pcn <> ''
),

drfi_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('drfi-', CAST(id AS VARCHAR(20)))           AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(pcn))                                   AS pcn_linkage,
        'Debt Recovery Failed Instalment'                  AS lba_type,
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))                          AS lba_template,
        datesent                                           AS lba_issue_date,
        batchid                                            AS batch_id,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                  AS written_off,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                  AS solicitors,
        'drfi'                                              AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('drfi') }}
    WHERE pcn IS NOT NULL AND pcn <> ''
),

dr_returned_post_ccj_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('dr_returned_post_ccj-', CAST(id AS VARCHAR(20))) AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(pcn))                                         AS pcn_linkage,
        'Post-CCJ Debt Recovery Returned'                        AS lba_type,
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))                                AS lba_template,
        COALESCE(datereturned, dateadded)                        AS lba_issue_date,
        batchid                                                  AS batch_id,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                        AS written_off,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                        AS solicitors,
        'dr_returned_post_ccj'                                   AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('dr_returned_post_ccj') }}
    WHERE pcn IS NOT NULL AND pcn <> ''
),

cpr_letters_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('cpr_letters-', CAST(cl.id AS VARCHAR(20)))  AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(cl.pcn))                                 AS pcn_linkage,
        COALESCE(lkp.lba_type, 'CPR Letter')                AS lba_type,
        lkp.lba_template                                    AS lba_template,
        cl.datesent                                         AS lba_issue_date,
        cl.batch                                            AS batch_id,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                   AS written_off,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                   AS solicitors,
        'cpr_letters'                                        AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('cpr_letters') }} cl
    LEFT JOIN letter_type_lookup lkp ON lkp.template_id = cl.templateid
    WHERE cl.pcn IS NOT NULL AND cl.pcn <> ''
),

cpr_letter_new_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('cpr_letter_new-', CAST(cn.id AS VARCHAR(20))) AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(cn.pcn))                                   AS pcn_linkage,
        COALESCE(lkp.lba_type, 'CPR Letter (New)')            AS lba_type,
        lkp.lba_template                                      AS lba_template,
        cn.dateadded                                          AS lba_issue_date,
        cn.batch                                              AS batch_id,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                     AS written_off,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                     AS solicitors,
        'cpr_letter_new'                                       AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('cpr_letter_new') }} cn
    LEFT JOIN letter_type_lookup lkp ON lkp.template_id = cn.templateid
    WHERE cn.pcn IS NOT NULL AND cn.pcn <> ''
),

-- no_send_court carries no id column at all -- pcn + dateadded is the
-- natural key.
no_send_court_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('no_send_court-', TRIM(UPPER(pcn)), '-',
               CAST(dateadded AS VARCHAR(30)))     AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(pcn))                           AS pcn_linkage,
        'No Send Court'                            AS lba_type,
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))                  AS lba_template,
        dateadded                                  AS lba_issue_date,
        CAST(NULL AS INT)                          AS batch_id,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                          AS written_off,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                          AS solicitors,
        'no_send_court'                             AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('no_send_court') }}
    WHERE pcn IS NOT NULL AND pcn <> ''
),

pcn_no_further_action_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('pcn_no_further_action-', CAST(id AS VARCHAR(20))) AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(pcn))                                          AS pcn_linkage,
        'PCN No Further Action'                                   AS lba_type,
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))                                 AS lba_template,
        datenoaction                                              AS lba_issue_date,
        CAST(NULL AS INT)                                         AS batch_id,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                         AS written_off,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                         AS solicitors,
        'pcn_no_further_action'                                   AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('pcn_no_further_action') }}
    WHERE pcn IS NOT NULL AND pcn <> ''
),

pcn_application_set_aside_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('pcn_application_set_aside-', CAST(id AS VARCHAR(20))) AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(pcn))                                              AS pcn_linkage,
        'PCN Application Set Aside'                                   AS lba_type,
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))                                     AS lba_template,
        dateadded                                                     AS lba_issue_date,
        CAST(NULL AS INT)                                             AS batch_id,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                             AS written_off,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                             AS solicitors,
        'pcn_application_set_aside'                                    AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('pcn_application_set_aside') }}
    WHERE pcn IS NOT NULL AND pcn <> ''
),

scottish_pre_legal_wp_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('scottish_pre_legal_wp-', CAST(sp.id AS VARCHAR(20))) AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(sp.pcn))                                          AS pcn_linkage,
        COALESCE(lkp.lba_type, 'Scottish Pre-Legal WP')              AS lba_type,
        lkp.lba_template                                             AS lba_template,
        sp.datesent                                                  AS lba_issue_date,
        sp.batchid                                                   AS batch_id,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                            AS written_off,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                            AS solicitors,
        'scottish_pre_legal_wp'                                       AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('scottish_pre_legal_wp') }} sp
    LEFT JOIN letter_type_lookup lkp ON lkp.template_id = sp.templateid
    WHERE sp.pcn IS NOT NULL AND sp.pcn <> ''
),

debt_recovery_scottish_lba_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('debt_recovery_scottish_lba-', CAST(id AS VARCHAR(20))) AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(pcn))                                               AS pcn_linkage,
        'Debt Recovery / LBA (Scotland)'                               AS lba_type,
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))                                      AS lba_template,
        debt_recovery_date                                             AS lba_issue_date,
        batch_id                                                       AS batch_id,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                              AS written_off,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                              AS solicitors,
        'debt_recovery_scottish_lba'                                   AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('debt_recovery_scottish_lba') }}
    WHERE pcn IS NOT NULL AND pcn <> ''
),

-- 6. Debt Recovery Post CCJ / Post CCJ WP Offer -- client-confirmed
--    2026-09-04: `Staging.ReportPCNMonthlyCurrent2`'s ladder flags
--    (FirstReminderSent, SecondReminderSent, DebtRecovery1stPlacement,
--    PostCCJReminder, PostCCJLetter, PostCCJWPEnfLetter) are each just "is
--    this PCN present in the respective table" -- no hidden aggregation
--    logic. That confirmation is what unblocks wiring these into
--    int_pcn_event_scd_legacy.sql's ladder (see that file's header).
--    debt_recovery_post_ccj was already staged (pre-dates this addition)
--    but had never been unioned into this model.
debt_recovery_post_ccj_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('debt_recovery_post_ccj-', CAST(id AS VARCHAR(20))) AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(pcn))                                           AS pcn_linkage,
        'Debt Recovery Post CCJ'                                   AS lba_type,
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))                                  AS lba_template,
        debt_recovery_date                                         AS lba_issue_date,
        batch_id                                                   AS batch_id,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                          AS written_off,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                          AS solicitors,
        'debt_recovery_post_ccj'                                   AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('debt_recovery_post_ccj') }}
    WHERE pcn IS NOT NULL AND pcn <> ''
),

-- `vwpostccj` (client view, decoded 2026-09-04) = postccj UNION postccjwp
-- UNION postccjwp2 UNION postccjwp3 -- "Post CCJ WP Offer" is presence in
-- that same combined set, so all three WP batches count, each its own
-- labelled stream here (postccj itself has no separate ladder stage; its
-- WP follow-up letters are the milestone).
post_ccj_wp_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('post_ccj_wp-', CAST(w.id AS VARCHAR(20)))   AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(w.pcn))                                  AS pcn_linkage,
        COALESCE(lkp.lba_type, 'Post CCJ WP Offer')          AS lba_type,
        lkp.lba_template                                    AS lba_template,
        w.date_sent                                         AS lba_issue_date,
        w.batch_id                                          AS batch_id,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                   AS written_off,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                   AS solicitors,
        'post_ccj_wp'                                        AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('post_ccj_wp') }} w
    LEFT JOIN letter_type_lookup lkp ON lkp.template_id = w.template_id
    WHERE w.pcn IS NOT NULL AND w.pcn <> ''
),

post_ccj_wp_2_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('post_ccj_wp_2-', CAST(w.id AS VARCHAR(20))) AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(w.pcn))                                  AS pcn_linkage,
        COALESCE(lkp.lba_type, 'Post CCJ WP Offer')          AS lba_type,
        lkp.lba_template                                    AS lba_template,
        w.date_sent                                         AS lba_issue_date,
        w.batch_id                                          AS batch_id,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                   AS written_off,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                   AS solicitors,
        'post_ccj_wp_2'                                      AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('post_ccj_wp_2') }} w
    LEFT JOIN letter_type_lookup lkp ON lkp.template_id = w.template_id
    WHERE w.pcn IS NOT NULL AND w.pcn <> ''
),

post_ccj_wp_3_events AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('post_ccj_wp_3-', CAST(w.id AS VARCHAR(20))) AS lba_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(w.pcn))                                  AS pcn_linkage,
        COALESCE(lkp.lba_type, 'Post CCJ WP Offer')          AS lba_type,
        lkp.lba_template                                    AS lba_template,
        w.date_sent                                         AS lba_issue_date,
        w.batch_id                                          AS batch_id,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                   AS written_off,
        CAST(NULL AS BIT)                                   AS solicitors,
        'post_ccj_wp_3'                                      AS lba_source_table
    FROM {{ ref('post_ccj_wp_3') }} w
    LEFT JOIN letter_type_lookup lkp ON lkp.template_id = w.template_id
    WHERE w.pcn IS NOT NULL AND w.pcn <> ''
),

final AS (
    SELECT * FROM lba_reminder_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM non_pofa_2_reminder_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM third_reminder_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM post_ccj_reminder_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM post_ccj_14_days_reminder_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM reminders_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM reminders_pofa_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM debt_recovery_lba_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM debt_recovery_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM debt_recovery_2_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM dr_returned_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM dr_returned_2_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM drfi_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM dr_returned_post_ccj_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM cpr_letters_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM cpr_letter_new_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM no_send_court_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM pcn_no_further_action_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM pcn_application_set_aside_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM scottish_pre_legal_wp_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM debt_recovery_scottish_lba_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM debt_recovery_post_ccj_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM post_ccj_wp_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM post_ccj_wp_2_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM post_ccj_wp_3_events
)

SELECT * FROM final

model.ccp.core_payment_attempt_failed_le.name: core_payment_attempt_failed_legacy
model.ccp.core_payment_attempt_failed_le.raw_code:
-- Core payment-attempt-failed entity (Built from Traffic Guard
-- declinedpayments). Grain = 1 per failed payment attempt (7,893,911 rows).
-- Per context.md §2.6/§10 #5.
--
-- Deliberately NOT part of core_payment_legacy -- every row here is a FAILED
-- attempt: money that never arrived. It is 2.9x the size of `payments` and
-- 1.9x the entire PCN population, so unioning it into core_payment_legacy
-- would make 71% of that table non-payments and inflate every amount
-- measure by roughly 3x (context.md §10 defect #5).
--
-- Its amounts are in the right unit (mean 87.62, max 882, alongside
-- `payments` at mean 60.60) -- this is a semantic exclusion from
-- core_payment_legacy, not a units problem.
--
-- Repeated card failures are a genuine collections signal -- surface this as
-- a COUNT per PCN wherever consumed, never as an amount in a payment fact
-- (context.md §2.6).
--
-- Naming: TrafficGuard/NewLogic (legacy-system) core entity -- see the naming
-- note in core_claim_legacy.sql.

{{ config(
    alias = 'core_payment_attempt_failed_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'payment']
) }}

SELECT
    id                      AS payment_attempt_id,
    {{ pcn_key('pcn') }}    AS pcn_id,
    my_date                 AS attempted_at,
    amount                  AS attempted_amount,
    reason                  AS decline_reason,
    vendor_tx_code

FROM {{ ref('declined_payments') }}
WHERE pcn IS NOT NULL AND pcn <> ''

model.ccp.core_payment_legacy.name: core_payment_legacy
model.ccp.core_payment_legacy.raw_code:
-- Core payment entity (Built from Traffic Guard payments + sagepaypayments +
-- manualpayments, UNIONed with a payment_channel discriminator). Per
-- context.md §2.6 core__payment.
--
-- [see original header for the channel / double-count / declinedpayments notes]
--
-- claim_payment_stage (added): pre_court / post_court / refund, mirroring
-- core_payment's Zeus-side flag. post_court uses the SAME qualifying
-- condition core_claim_legacy applies for post_court_cash_collected
-- (payment_date >= claim_issue_date), so the two reconcile by construction.
--
-- The claim issue date is derived INLINE below from court_issued + violators
-- rather than ref'ing core_claim_legacy: that model is downstream of this one
-- via core_pcn_legacy, so ref'ing it closes a dbt cycle
-- (core_claim_legacy --> core_payment_legacy --> core_pcn_legacy -->
-- core_claim_legacy). The logic is copied verbatim from core_claim_legacy.sql's
-- `base` CTE -- if that changes, change it here too.
--
-- Legacy has no refund flag, so a negative amount is the only refund signal
-- available -- note manual_channel already ceilings to 0-10,000, so refunds
-- can only ever surface on the payments/sagepay channels.

{{ config(
    alias = 'core_payment_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'payment']
) }}

WITH

payments_channel AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('payments-', CAST(p.id AS VARCHAR(20)))  AS payment_id,
        {{ pcn_key('p.pcn') }}                           AS pcn_id,
        CAST(p.amount AS DECIMAL(19,4))                  AS amount,
        p.received                                       AS payment_date,
        COALESCE(pm.method_name, p.method)               AS payment_method,
        p.method                                         AS payment_method_raw,
        p.pcn_stage                                      AS channel_status,
        'payments'                                       AS payment_channel,
        1                                                AS is_successful
    FROM {{ ref('payments') }} p
    LEFT JOIN {{ ref('tg_payment_method_normalise') }} pm ON pm.raw_method = p.method
    WHERE p.pcn IS NOT NULL AND p.pcn <> ''
      AND p.amount <> 0
      -- DATA QUALITY 2026-09-22: 2 rows have received IS NULL in TG payments.
      -- Rows are KEPT (no createdon equivalent in TG payments table).
      -- payment_date / days_since_issue will be NULL for these 2 rows only;
      -- they remain in the table for future cash reconciliation.
),

sagepay_channel AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('sagepay-', CAST(id AS VARCHAR(20)))    AS payment_id,
        {{ pcn_key('pcn') }}                            AS pcn_id,
        CAST(amount AS DECIMAL(19,4))                   AS amount,
        created_at                                      AS payment_date,
        'SagePay'                                       AS payment_method,
        'SagePay'                                       AS payment_method_raw,
        final_status                                    AS channel_status,
        'sagepay'                                       AS payment_channel,
        1                                               AS is_successful
    FROM {{ ref('sage_pay_payments') }}
    WHERE pcn IS NOT NULL AND pcn <> ''
      AND amount <> 0
),

-- context.md §10 #6 (defect): manualpayments.amount is NOT safe to sum
-- as-is -- 9,030 rows, mean 162,424.56, MAX 1,465,891,979.00 against a
-- maximum PCN charge of 1,800.00. Ceiling it at a defensible bound (0-10,000;
-- the bound itself is a §10 open item #2 business decision) and flag what
-- got rejected so the number is never silently wrong.
manual_channel AS (
    SELECT
        CONCAT('manual-', CAST(id AS VARCHAR(20)))     AS payment_id,
        {{ pcn_key('pcn') }}                            AS pcn_id,
        CASE WHEN amount BETWEEN 0 AND 10000 THEN CAST(amount AS DECIMAL(19,4)) END AS amount,
        date                                            AS payment_date,
        'Manual'                                        AS payment_method,
        'Manual'                                        AS payment_method_raw,
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(100))                      AS channel_status,
        'manual'                                        AS payment_channel,
        CASE WHEN amount BETWEEN 0 AND 10000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_successful
    FROM {{ ref('manual_payments') }}
    WHERE pcn IS NOT NULL AND pcn <> ''
      AND amount <> 0
),

-- context.md §10 #5 (defect): declinedpayments is deliberately EXCLUDED.
-- 7,893,911 rows -- 2.9x `payments`, 1.9x the entire PCN population -- every
-- one a FAILED attempt. Unioning it in made 71% of this table non-payments
-- and inflated every amount measure by roughly 3x. Modelled separately at
-- its own grain in core_payment_attempt_failed_legacy instead.
combined AS (
    SELECT * FROM payments_channel
    UNION ALL SELECT * FROM sagepay_channel
    UNION ALL SELECT * FROM manual_channel
),

-- Court claims, claim-grain, straight off court_issued. The
-- violators.claim IS NOT NULL gate is carried over deliberately -- see
-- core_claim_legacy.sql's header for the confirmed live 2026-09-08 overcount
-- (1 extra claim / £170 for Feb 2023) it prevents, and the aliasing trap:
-- violators has its OWN pcn column, so the EXISTS must reference ci.pcn
-- explicitly or SQL Server silently resolves the bare name to violators.pcn.
claim_base AS (
    SELECT
        ci.id                                           AS claim_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(CAST(ci.pcn AS VARCHAR(50))))        AS pcn_id,
        COALESCE(ci.date_claim_obtained, ci.datetime)   AS claim_issue_date

    FROM {{ ref('court_issued') }} AS ci

    WHERE ci.pcn IS NOT NULL
      AND TRIM(CAST(ci.pcn AS VARCHAR(50))) <> ''
      AND EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM {{ ref('violators') }} v
          WHERE TRIM(UPPER(CAST(v.full_pcn AS VARCHAR(50)))) = TRIM(UPPER(CAST(ci.pcn AS VARCHAR(50))))
            AND v.claim IS NOT NULL
      )
),

-- A PCN can carry more than one court claim over time; rank to the latest so
-- the join below cannot fan out payment rows.
claim_latest AS (
    SELECT
        pcn_id,
        claim_id,
        claim_issue_date
    FROM (
        SELECT
            pcn_id,
            claim_id,
            claim_issue_date,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
                PARTITION BY pcn_id
                ORDER BY claim_issue_date DESC, claim_id DESC
            ) AS rn
        FROM claim_base
        WHERE claim_issue_date IS NOT NULL
    ) r
    WHERE rn = 1
)

SELECT
    c.payment_id,
    c.pcn_id,
    c.amount,
    c.payment_date,
    c.payment_method,
    c.payment_method_raw,
    c.channel_status,
    c.payment_channel,
    c.is_successful,

    -- [NEW] Court claim context
    CAST(cl.claim_id AS VARCHAR(100))       AS claim_id,
    CAST(cl.claim_issue_date AS DATE)       AS claim_issue_date,

    -- [UPDATED] refunds netted into post_court/pre_court by payment_date,
    -- not carved into a separate 'refund' stage -- mirrors core_payment.sql
    -- (Zeus); see that model for the Per CCP July-2026 evidence.
    CAST(
        CASE
            WHEN cl.claim_issue_date IS NOT NULL
             AND CAST(c.payment_date AS DATE) >= CAST(cl.claim_issue_date AS DATE)
                THEN 'post_court'
            ELSE 'pre_court'
        END
        AS VARCHAR(20)
    )                                       AS claim_payment_stage

FROM combined c

LEFT JOIN claim_latest cl
    ON cl.pcn_id = c.pcn_id

model.ccp.core_payment_plan_legacy.name: core_payment_plan_legacy
model.ccp.core_payment_plan_legacy.raw_code:
-- Core payment plan entity (Built from Traffic Guard installmentconfig,
-- enriched with installment + paymentplantype). Grain = 1 per instalment
-- plan. Per context.md §6.3 core__payment_plan.
--
-- Naming: TrafficGuard/NewLogic (legacy-system) core entity -- see the naming
-- note in core_claim_legacy.sql.
--
-- Extremely sparse (0.025% of PCNs, per context.md) -- expect
-- payment_plan_type to carry no real information (⚠️ all 'Legal', 1 distinct
-- value confirmed in context.md §9 rule 2's "populated but constant" list).
-- Build it anyway; sparse ≠ broken (§9 rule 3).

{{ config(
    alias = 'core_payment_plan_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'payment']
) }}

WITH

installments_agg AS (
    SELECT
        installment_config_id,
        COUNT(*)          AS installments_recorded,
        SUM(paid_amount)  AS total_paid_via_installments
    FROM {{ ref('installment') }}
    GROUP BY installment_config_id
)

SELECT
    ic.id                       AS payment_plan_id,
    {{ pcn_key('ic.pcn') }}     AS pcn_id,
    ic.total_amount             AS plan_total_amount,
    ic.number_of_installment    AS number_of_installments,
    ic.installment_amount       AS installment_amount,
    ic.added_date                AS plan_start_date,
    ic.active                   AS active_flag,
    ic.completed                AS completed_flag,
    pt.name                     AS payment_plan_type,   -- low-info: all 'Legal' per context.md, kept for completeness
    ia.installments_recorded,
    ia.total_paid_via_installments

FROM {{ ref('installment_config') }} ic
LEFT JOIN {{ ref('payment_plan_type') }} pt ON pt.id = ic.payment_plan_type_id
LEFT JOIN installments_agg ia               ON ia.installment_config_id = ic.id
WHERE ic.pcn IS NOT NULL
  AND ic.pcn <> ''

model.ccp.core_pcn_legacy.name: core_pcn_legacy
model.ccp.core_pcn_legacy.raw_code:
-- Core PCN entity (Built from Traffic Guard violators + enrichment/decodes).
-- Grain = 1 per PCN (violators.fullPCN, ~4,137,094 rows) -- the central entity
-- of the whole legacy estate; almost everything else joins back to this.
-- Assembled per context.md §6.3 (core__pcn feeds) and §7.1 (fact_pcn column
-- spec) -- read those before changing this model.
--
-- Naming: TrafficGuard/NewLogic (legacy-system) core entity -- see the naming
-- note in core_claim_legacy.sql. Plain core__pcn is reserved for the eventual
-- conformed entity if/when this is unioned with a live Zeus-side equivalent.
--
-- Carries all three PCN-ish keys per context.md §4.1, none re-derived downstream:
--   pcn_id       = violators.fullPCN (the business key -- use this to join out)
--   pcn_short    = violators.PCN (older/shorter form -- Reminders tables only)
--   violator_sk  = violators.ID (int surrogate -- violators_appeal/addresschanges/
--                  pcnticketpricelog join on this, not on either PCN form)
--
-- Scope boundaries (do not expand this model beyond them):
--   - dni_status/dni_reason (noAction) are NOT wired up here -- context.md
--     names noAction.notAtAddress as the source but documents no join key back
--     to violators/PCN anywhere, and noaction's own columns (noActionId,
--     letterId, dateAdded, userId) don't obviously carry one either. Emitted
--     as explicit NULLs rather than guessing a join (context.md §13 rule 1).
--     (pcnonhold, previously in the same boat pending a lakehouse shortcut,
--     was wired up 2026-08-17 once the shortcut was added.)
--   - appeal_status, tracing_status, claim_status, lba_status/lba_type,
--     payment_plan_type/_start_date are resolved as FK lookups at the fact
--     layer against their own core/intermediate entities (core_appeal_legacy
--     + int_appeal_outcome_legacy, core_tracing_legacy, core_claim_legacy,
--     core_lba_legacy, core_payment_plan_legacy) -- not duplicated here.
--     lba_status specifically comes from int_collection_stage_legacy
--     (current position), a different question from "was an LBA ever sent"
--     (core_lba_legacy/fact_lba) -- see fact_pcn_legacy.sql.
--   - discount_flag/discount_amount are NOT built here. context.md §4.2
--     measured violators.reducedamount non-zero on 99.95% of records -- it is
--     the standard early-payment price, not a discount marker. The real,
--     four-signal derivation lives in int_discount_flag_legacy; consume that
--     instead of guessing from a column on this table.
--
-- Per context.md §9 rule 1, every pcn/registration-shaped join key is
-- TRIM/UPPER-normalised.

{{ config(
    alias = 'core_pcn_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'pcn']
) }}

WITH

-- 1. Anchor: one row per PCN.
base AS (
    SELECT
        id                                              AS violator_sk,
        TRIM(UPPER(full_pcn))                          AS pcn_id,
        TRIM(UPPER(pcn))                                AS pcn_short,
        TRIM(UPPER(registration))                       AS registration,
        TRIM(UPPER(site))                               AS site_id,
        -- SCD2 spec item 13 RESOLVED 2026-09-03: the client's own view
        -- (Staging.viewFactTicketsSCD2) raises "Ticket Issued" from
        -- ORIGPCNSENT (the ORIGINAL send), not PCNSENT -- they differ on
        -- every reissued PCN (`Reissues` is a live pcnstatus value, 310,398
        -- PCNs affected). issue_date now follows that same convention.
        -- orig_pcn_sent_date used over the sibling orig_pcn_sent column --
        -- 100% populated (4,137,094/4,137,094) against the same values.
        orig_pcn_sent_date                              AS issue_date,
        -- The superseded pcn_sent value (may reflect a later reissue date)
        -- kept alongside rather than dropped -- not the canonical issue
        -- date anymore, but real information.
        pcn_sent                                        AS reissue_date,
        -- SCD2 spec item 5 (defect): the violation date -- item 14's event
        -- ladder needs this as event_type_order 1; the spine never carried
        -- it before.
        date_of_violation                               AS violation_date,
        -- SCD2 spec item 6/11: arrival_time is only present on an
        -- ANPR-captured ticket (95.0% populated, 3,929,690/4,137,094) --
        -- absence of it is itself the Manual/ANPR discriminator, not a gap.
        arrival_time,
        CAST(CASE WHEN arrival_time IS NULL THEN 'Manual' ELSE 'ANPR' END AS VARCHAR(10)) AS ticket_type,
        ticket_price                                    AS charge,
        pcn_status                                      AS current_status,
        pcn_status                                      AS payment_status,
        pcn_status_updated,
        fully_paid                                      AS fully_paid_flag,
        settled                                         AS fully_paid_date,
        amount_outstanding_cal,
        ticket_price                                    AS total_payment_amount,
        (ticket_price - amount_outstanding_cal)         AS total_paid,
        -- MEASURED (context.md §10 #4/defect 4): of 252,589 populated values,
        -- 0 cast to INT and 0 match courtissued.id, but 25,972 match
        -- defense.claimnumber -- this is the free-text COURT CLAIM NUMBER, a
        -- different key space from core_claim_legacy.claim_id (courtissued.id,
        -- an INT). Never join the two on this column.
        claim                                           AS court_claim_number,
        an_possible_violator_id,
        mv_group_id
    FROM {{ ref('violators') }}
    WHERE full_pcn IS NOT NULL
      AND full_pcn <> ''
),

-- 2. Cancelled: existence -> cancelled_flag (99.83% match per context.md §7.1).
cancelled_ranked AS (
    SELECT
        TRIM(UPPER(pcn))    AS pcn_id,
        reason              AS cancelled_reason,
        cancelled           AS cancelled_date,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY TRIM(UPPER(pcn))
            ORDER BY cancelled DESC
        ) AS rn
    FROM {{ ref('cancelled') }}
),

cancelled_latest AS (
    SELECT pcn_id, cancelled_reason, cancelled_date
    FROM cancelled_ranked
    WHERE rn = 1
),

-- 3. Paused (pcnonhold): 214 rows per context.md §7.1, rare-but-real per §9
--    rule 3. Was blocked until 2026-08-17 (table not yet mirrored into the
--    lakehouse); now live -- rank defensively in case a pcn was paused more
--    than once.
pcnonhold_ranked AS (
    SELECT
        TRIM(UPPER(pcn))    AS pcn_id,
        notes               AS paused_reason,
        date_on_hold        AS paused_date,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY TRIM(UPPER(pcn))
            ORDER BY date_on_hold DESC
        ) AS rn
    FROM {{ ref('pcn_on_hold') }}
),

pcnonhold_latest AS (
    SELECT pcn_id, paused_reason, paused_date
    FROM pcnonhold_ranked
    WHERE rn = 1
),

-- 4. Multiviolator group: joined on mv_group_id (NOT pcn/registration).
--    mvGroups has no type/category column -- existence only (context.md §7.1).
mvgroups_flag AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT mv_group_id
    FROM {{ ref('mv_groups') }}
    WHERE mv_group_id IS NOT NULL
),

-- 5. Repeat offender: the client-confirmed rule is the THIRD DVLA enquiry
--    onwards for a registration, built in int_repeat_offender_legacy over
--    dvlarep (dvla = registration, offenceDate = the enquiry date).
--    This previously used the `repeat_offenders` table -- 4,099 rows over
--    1,082 registrations, against 159,171 under the confirmed rule, a 147x
--    difference, so the old table was not this population at all.
--    Rolled up to one row per registration because that model is
--    enquiry-grained and would otherwise fan out the 4,137,094-row spine.
repeat_offender_latest AS (
    SELECT reg, MAX(CAST(repeat_offender_status AS TINYINT)) AS repeat_offender_status
    FROM {{ ref('int_repeat_offender_legacy') }}
    GROUP BY reg
),

-- 6. Potential-violation link: joined on an_possible_violator_id = id
--    (an int FK, not a pcn/registration join). Only 25.3% match per
--    context.md §7.1 -- expected, not a defect.
pv_match AS (
    SELECT id AS pv_id
    FROM {{ ref('an_possible_violators') }}
),

-- 7. Real payment total, from actual transaction events -- NOT
-- (ticket_price - amount_outstanding_cal) (context.md §10 open item #5:
-- "total_paid is derived, not stored"). amount_outstanding_cal is whatever
-- the client's own system last computed as outstanding and can drift out of
-- sync with the real transaction history. Confirmed live 2026-09-09 against
-- the client's own Accrued Income Report: the derived figure overstates
-- actual collections by ~2x (April 2023 cohort: £3.29M derived vs £1.68M
-- report vs £1.68M from this event-level rebuild, within 0.13%). Same
-- TG/Zeus precedence and scoping as int_pcn_event_scd_legacy.sql's own
-- "Ticket Payment" branches -- a migrated ticket's TG payment record is
-- suppressed once it has ANY Dynamics presence at all, and only Zeus
-- payments for TG-originated tickets are in scope here (this is the legacy
-- spine; a Zeus-native ticket has no TG row to attach to).
tg_payments AS (
    SELECT p.pcn_id, p.amount
    FROM {{ ref('core_payment_legacy') }} p
    WHERE p.payment_date IS NOT NULL
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM {{ ref('incident') }} i
          WHERE i.parentcaseid IS NULL AND i.ccp_ticketno IS NOT NULL
            AND TRIM(UPPER(i.ccp_ticketno)) = p.pcn_id
      )
),

zeus_payments AS (
    SELECT z.pcn_ticket_no AS pcn_id, z.amount_delta AS amount
    FROM {{ ref('int_ticket_payment_zeus') }} z
    WHERE z.payment_date IS NOT NULL
      AND EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM {{ ref('violators') }} v
          WHERE TRIM(UPPER(v.full_pcn)) = z.pcn_ticket_no
      )
),

payment_totals AS (
    SELECT
        pcn_id,
        SUM(amount) AS total_paid_events,
        -- Gross "ever paid" signal -- see core_pcn.sql's ever_paid_flag
        -- (same fix, mirrored here for Legacy) for the full derivation.
        -- Matches the client's TicketWasPaid semantics: any nonzero
        -- transaction row, positive or negative, not a net-positive-balance
        -- test.
        COUNT(CASE WHEN amount <> 0 THEN 1 END) AS n_nonzero_transactions
    FROM (
        SELECT pcn_id, amount FROM tg_payments
        UNION ALL
        SELECT pcn_id, amount FROM zeus_payments
    ) combined
    GROUP BY pcn_id
),

final AS (
    SELECT
        b.violator_sk,
        b.pcn_id,
        b.pcn_short,
        b.registration,
        b.site_id,
        b.issue_date,
        b.reissue_date,
        b.violation_date,
        b.arrival_time,
        b.ticket_type,
        b.charge,
        b.current_status,
        b.payment_status,
        b.pcn_status_updated,
        b.fully_paid_flag,
        b.fully_paid_date,
        b.amount_outstanding_cal,
        b.total_payment_amount,
        CAST(COALESCE(pt.total_paid_events, 0) AS DECIMAL(18,2)) AS total_paid,
        CAST(CASE WHEN COALESCE(pt.n_nonzero_transactions, 0) > 0
                  THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS BIT) AS ever_paid_flag,
        b.court_claim_number,

        CAST(CASE WHEN c.pcn_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS BIT) AS cancelled_flag,
        c.cancelled_reason,
        c.cancelled_date,

        CAST(CASE WHEN poh.pcn_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS BIT) AS paused_flag,
        poh.paused_reason,
        poh.paused_date,

        CASE WHEN mvg.mv_group_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'MV' ELSE 'SV' END AS multiviolator_type,

        'Non-Fuzzy' AS match_type,  -- no fuzzy signal exists in legacy (context.md §7.1)

        CASE
            WHEN COALESCE(b.issue_date, b.reissue_date) IS NULL
                THEN NULL
            WHEN MONTH(COALESCE(b.issue_date, b.reissue_date)) >= 4
                THEN CONCAT('FY', RIGHT(CAST(YEAR(COALESCE(b.issue_date, b.reissue_date)) + 1 AS VARCHAR(4)), 2))
            ELSE CONCAT('FY', RIGHT(CAST(YEAR(COALESCE(b.issue_date, b.reissue_date)) AS VARCHAR(4)), 2))
        END AS issue_fy,

        -- No PCN-grain fuzzy signal exists in legacy -- the only fuzzy data is
        -- record_type IN ('FUZZY','FUZZYNOPARK') at stream/read grain, and
        -- reaching PCN grain from there needs the NewLogic-pair-to-TrafficGuard
        -- link, which is unresolved (see fact_pv.sql's note on
        -- fuzzy_permit_flag). Defaults to Non-fuzzy per confirmed decision
        -- (2026-09-02) until that link exists.
        CASE WHEN mvg.mv_group_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'Non-fuzzy MV' ELSE 'Non-fuzzy SV' END AS type_label,

        CAST(ISNULL(ro.repeat_offender_status, 0) AS BIT) AS repeat_offender_status,

        pv.pv_id,

        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50)) AS dni_status,  -- no documented join path from noAction back to a pcn/violator; context.md §7.1 + header note
        CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(250)) AS dni_reason, -- no source anywhere; context.md §7.1

        -- 11,877 PCNs carry a negative amount_outstanding_cal (refund, fee
        -- reversal, or error -- unconfirmed). Never clamp; expose raw and flag.
        CAST(CASE WHEN b.amount_outstanding_cal < 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS BIT) AS overpaid_flag,
        CAST(CASE WHEN COALESCE(pt.total_paid_events, 0) < 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS BIT) AS total_paid_negative_flag


    FROM base b
    LEFT JOIN cancelled_latest c        ON c.pcn_id = b.pcn_id
    LEFT JOIN pcnonhold_latest poh      ON poh.pcn_id = b.pcn_id
    LEFT JOIN mvgroups_flag mvg         ON mvg.mv_group_id = b.mv_group_id
    LEFT JOIN repeat_offender_latest ro ON ro.reg = b.registration
    LEFT JOIN payment_totals pt         ON pt.pcn_id = b.pcn_id
    LEFT JOIN pv_match pv               ON pv.pv_id = b.an_possible_violator_id
)

SELECT * ,            CONVERT(
        VARCHAR(32),
        HASHBYTES(
            'MD5',
            CONCAT(
                UPPER(LTRIM(RTRIM(multiviolator_type))),
                '|',
                UPPER(LTRIM(RTRIM(match_type)))
            )
        ),
        2
    ) AS violation_type_key FROM final

model.ccp.core_pcn_lifecycle_legacy.name: core_pcn_lifecycle_legacy
model.ccp.core_pcn_lifecycle_legacy.raw_code:
-- Core PCN lifecycle entity (TrafficGuard/Legacy).
-- Grain = 1 row per PCN per lifecycle stage genuinely reached.
--
-- Mirrors core_pcn_lifecycle.sql's (Zeus) output shape so both sides union
-- cleanly in fact_pcn_lifecycle.sql -- but built on real event history
-- (int_pcn_event_scd_legacy, itself sourced from the client's own SCD2
-- ladder logic), not a current-snapshot table. That means, unlike the Zeus
-- version, stage_end_date here is a real value for every stage except the
-- ticket's current/open one -- see int_pcn_event_scd_legacy.sql's header
-- for why the Zeus side can't do this (int_incident_deduped only carries
-- the latest snapshot per ticket, so its LEAD()-based stage_end_date is
-- always NULL in practice).
--
-- Only rows with a resolved stage_key are kept -- int_pcn_event_scd_legacy
-- also carries Violation/Ticket Payment/Ticket Cancellation as event-grain
-- rows for running_total_paid purposes, but those are financial/lifecycle
-- events layered on the ladder, not escalation stages themselves (same
-- distinction that model's own is_stage flag makes).
--
-- stage_end_date is recomputed here, NOT passed through from
-- int_pcn_event_scd_legacy directly -- that model's own stage_end_date is
-- LEAD()'d over the FULL event stream (stages + Payment/Cancellation
-- interleaved), so a payment landing right after a ticket's last real stage
-- truncates that stage's window to end right before the payment, leaving
-- the payment itself falling in a dead gap after the window and before any
-- (nonexistent) next stage -- confirmed live 2026-09-16: this is exactly
-- why fact_payment.stage_at_payment_key stayed NULL for the vast majority
-- of Legacy payments even after wiring this model in. Recomputing
-- stage_end_date via LEAD() over the stage-only rows (using event_order,
-- which stays correctly ordered relative to the interleaved non-stage
-- events) fixes it: the true last stage per PCN now correctly gets a NULL
-- (open) end date, and every payment falls inside some stage's window.

{{ config(
    alias = 'core_pcn_lifecycle_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'legacy', 'pcn_lifecycle']
) }}

WITH stage_events AS (

    SELECT
        pcn_id,
        event_order,
        stage_key,
        stage_start_date,
        running_total_paid
    FROM {{ ref('int_pcn_event_scd_legacy') }}
    WHERE stage_key IS NOT NULL

),

stage_events_windowed AS (

    SELECT
        s.*,
        LEAD(s.stage_start_date) OVER (
            PARTITION BY s.pcn_id ORDER BY s.event_order
        ) AS next_stage_start_date
    FROM stage_events s

)

SELECT
    e.pcn_id,
    p.site_id,
    CAST(p.pcn_id AS VARCHAR(100))                          AS fine_id,

    e.stage_key,
    e.stage_start_date                                      AS stage_date,
    p.issue_date,

    -- Every row here is, by construction, a stage the ticket actually
    -- reached (an event genuinely recorded against it) -- unlike Zeus's
    -- reached_flag, which has to reconstruct this from separate
    -- sent-confirmation columns since its source has no per-stage event
    -- history to draw on.
    CAST(1 AS BIT)                                          AS reached_flag,

    CAST(
        CASE WHEN COALESCE(e.running_total_paid, 0) > 0
              OR p.fully_paid_flag = 1
             THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
    AS BIT)                                                  AS paid_at_stage_flag,

    CAST(COALESCE(e.running_total_paid, 0) AS DECIMAL(18,2)) AS cash_at_stage,
    CAST(NULL AS DECIMAL(18,2))                              AS amount_paid,  -- stage events carry no payment delta of their own; see cash_at_stage for cumulative cash

    p.charge                                                 AS total_payment_amount,

    e.stage_start_date,
    CASE WHEN e.next_stage_start_date IS NOT NULL
         THEN DATEADD(millisecond, -1, e.next_stage_start_date)
         ELSE NULL END                                       AS stage_end_date,  -- NULL on the ticket's true current/open stage

    CAST(COALESCE(df.discount_flag, 0) AS BIT)              AS discount_flag,
    df.discount_amount, 
    CASE 
        WHEN fully_paid_flag = 0 AND cancelled_flag = 0 THEN 1 
        ELSE 0 
    END                                                     AS is_live

FROM stage_events_windowed e
LEFT JOIN {{ ref('core_pcn_legacy') }} p
    ON p.pcn_id = e.pcn_id
LEFT JOIN {{ ref('int_discount_flag_legacy') }} df
    ON df.pcn_id = e.pcn_id

model.ccp.core_site_legacy.name: core_site_legacy
model.ccp.core_site_legacy.raw_code:
-- Core site entity (Built from Traffic Guard `Site Information`, enriched
-- with sitetypes/sitecategorytracking/sitereason/clientadminsites/
-- tablet_sites+groups/clientusers+clientusersites). Grain = 1 per site
-- (3,911 per context.md §7.11). Per context.md §6.1 core__site.
--
-- Naming: TrafficGuard/NewLogic (legacy-system) core entity -- see the naming
-- note in core_claim_legacy.sql.
--
-- site_nature prefers sitecategorytracking.category (26.66% null) OVER
-- Site Information.nature_of_site (65.5% null) -- context.md §9 rule 5.
-- sitecategorytracking is month/year-grained -- latest row per site.
--
-- monthly_free_cancel_budget: maxcancellations is per client-portal-user via
-- clientusersites, and a site can have several users. Context.md §11 #8
-- flags the rollup rule as an OPEN business decision ("which value wins?").
-- MAX is used here as a clearly-flagged default (most permissive reading),
-- not a resolved answer -- revisit once the business decides.
--
-- SECOND PASS (2026-08-31 dbt build guide -- dimension tables, second pass):
-- expanded to match a newer/fuller client ERD for dim_site. New joins:
-- site_terms (contract-term history, 81.4% coverage, preferred over Site
-- Information's own contractdate/contractend as a fallback),
-- sites_disabled_from_site_issued (a genuine site-DISABLE EVENT log --
-- previously missed because Site Information alone, a current-state
-- snapshot, could never hold event history).
--
-- quality_tier / quality_tier_rank: quality_tier draws from the SAME source
-- column as site_nature above (site_category_tracking.category) -- this is
-- flagged, not resolved: if the target ERD wants these as genuinely distinct
-- concepts, one of them has no real source yet. Kept as a deliberate
-- duplicate under two names, same pattern as fact_claims_legacy
-- .claim_stage_reason. quality_tier_rank maps FOUR tiers (Bronze=1/
-- Silver=2/Gold=3/Platinum=4), matching the live-side core_site.sql's own
-- confirmed CCP reporting-layer vocabulary -- whether TrafficGuard's
-- sitecategorytracking.category ever actually contains 'Platinum' is
-- unconfirmed; any unmapped value (a 5th tier, or a typo) still silently
-- falls to NULL, caught only by the dim's not_null/unique tests on the PK,
-- not on this column.
--
-- golive_date is a duplicate of live_date under the newer ERD's column name
-- -- live_date is kept unchanged (fact_site_lifecycle_legacy depends on it).
--
-- revenue_share_pct (site_transaction_charge) predates this pass and is left
-- as-is, but per this pass's own research this may be the WRONG source --
-- sitetransactioncharge/sitetransactionchargepnp read as a per-transaction
-- MONEY fee, not a percentage share. Not changed here (nothing currently
-- downstream reads it), flagged for business sign-off before trusting it.
--
-- renewal_date (date_of_the_latest_contract) and lost_date (the new
-- site-disable event log) are both BEST-CANDIDATE-ONLY, not confirmed
-- business-event dates. A second unreconciled candidate for renewal_date /
-- contract_start_date (dateofcurrentcontract) exists on Site Information but
-- is not used here. "Disabled" (lost_date) and "lost" (client relationship
-- ended) are not necessarily the same business event either.
--
-- spaces, size_band, size_band_sort, revenue_share_model, pcn_rev_share_band,
-- acquisition_date, acquisition_fy have NO source anywhere in TrafficGuard --
-- typed NULL, not guessed/derived.
--
-- clientadminsites cardinality per site was never profiled (unlike
-- site_terms/site_category_tracking, both confirmed genuinely multi-row) --
-- the existing "latest by id" dedup in client_admin_ranked below assumes
-- that's an acceptable pick if a site does turn out to have >1 client row.
--
-- THIRD PASS (2026-08-31, naming resolved -- reporting layer table
-- inventory): current_status now emits 'Live - operational' (disabled = 0)
-- / 'Disabled' (disabled = 1) / NULL (flag unset) instead of 'Active' --
-- the KPI definition tests Site Status = 'Live - operational', so 'Active'
-- would silently zero out the Live Sites KPI for every TrafficGuard site.
-- This asserts a TrafficGuard site that isn't disabled is equivalent to a
-- Zeus site that's live and operational -- plausible, unconfirmed.
--
-- latest_contract_length_years is a NEW bonus column (latest_contract_term)
-- paired with renewal_date, which already takes the LATEST contract date
-- (date_of_the_latest_contract) rather than the plain contract_date/
-- contract_term pairing used for contract_length_years above. Three
-- contract-length columns exist on Site Information in total (contract_term,
-- original_length_of_contract, latest_contract_term); only two are surfaced
-- here (contract_length_years pairs with contract_date/contract_end above,
-- latest_contract_length_years pairs with renewal_date) -- confirm which
-- pairing the target model actually wants before dropping either.
--
-- This model itself stays legacy-only (core stays split by source system,
-- per this project's own dbt_project.yml). The naming/merge resolution
-- (dropping the _legacy suffix, converging with the live core_site.sql
-- equivalent) happens one layer up, in the mart -- see dim_site.sql.

{{ config(
    alias = 'core_site_legacy',
    tags = ['core', 'site','core_site_legacy']
) }}

WITH

base AS (
    SELECT
        id                              AS site_sk,
        {{ pcn_key('site_code') }}      AS site_id,
        name_of_site                    AS site_name,
        region,
        postcode,
        disabled,
        disabled_letter,
        contract_date                   AS contract_start_date,
        contract_end                    AS contract_end_date,
        contract_term,
        has_been_renewed,
        category                        AS business_category,
        nature_of_site,
        site_type_id,
        first_pcn_sent_date,
        live_date,
        date_of_the_latest_contract     AS renewal_date,          -- best-candidate only, see header
        latest_contract_term,
        site_transaction_charge         AS revenue_share_pct,
        request_type                    AS site_sales_channel,
        podpoint_ref,
        cancellation_charge             AS free_cancellation_limit  -- context.md §2.10: [Site Information].cancellationcharge -- real, not a typed NULL
    FROM {{ ref('site_information') }}
    WHERE site_code IS NOT NULL
      AND site_code <> ''
),

site_type_decode AS (
    SELECT site_type_id, site_type AS site_rule_type, popla_prefix
    FROM {{ ref('site_types') }}
),

site_category_ranked AS (
    SELECT
        {{ pcn_key('site_code') }} AS site_id,
        category                    AS site_nature,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY {{ pcn_key('site_code') }}
            ORDER BY year DESC, month DESC
        ) AS rn
    FROM {{ ref('site_category_tracking') }}
),

site_category_latest AS (
    SELECT site_id, site_nature FROM site_category_ranked WHERE rn = 1
),

site_reason_ranked AS (
    SELECT
        {{ pcn_key('site') }}  AS site_id,
        reason                  AS status_sub_reason,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY {{ pcn_key('site') }} ORDER BY id DESC) AS rn
    FROM {{ ref('site_reason') }}
),

site_reason_latest AS (
    SELECT site_id, status_sub_reason FROM site_reason_ranked WHERE rn = 1
),

client_admin_ranked AS (
    SELECT
        {{ pcn_key('site_code') }} AS site_id,
        client_id                   AS customer_id,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY {{ pcn_key('site_code') }} ORDER BY id DESC) AS rn
    FROM {{ ref('client_admin_sites') }}
),

client_admin_latest AS (
    SELECT site_id, customer_id FROM client_admin_ranked WHERE rn = 1
),

-- genuine sequential contract-term history (81.4% of sites) -- "latest by
-- startdate" is an unconfirmed pick, same caveat class as every other
-- latest-row dedup in this model
site_terms_ranked AS (
    SELECT
        {{ pcn_key('site_code') }} AS site_id,
        start_date,
        end_date,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY {{ pcn_key('site_code') }}
            ORDER BY start_date DESC
        ) AS rn
    FROM {{ ref('site_terms') }}
),

site_terms_latest AS (
    SELECT site_id, start_date, end_date FROM site_terms_ranked WHERE rn = 1
),

-- real site-disable event log -- best candidate found for "when this site
-- was lost", see header
site_disabled_ranked AS (
    SELECT
        {{ pcn_key('site') }}  AS site_id,
        datetime                AS event_datetime,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY {{ pcn_key('site') }} ORDER BY datetime DESC) AS rn
    FROM {{ ref('sites_disabled_from_site_issued') }}
),

site_disabled_latest AS (
    SELECT site_id, event_datetime FROM site_disabled_ranked WHERE rn = 1
),

tablet_lookup AS (
    SELECT
        {{ pcn_key('ts.site') }} AS site_id,
        tsg.name                  AS tablet_type
    FROM {{ ref('tablet_sites') }} ts
    LEFT JOIN {{ ref('tablet_site_groups') }} tsg ON tsg.id = ts.group_id
),

-- Client-reported (2026-09-21): "484 TrafficGuard Site IDs which are
-- non-existent sites" / "98 TrafficGuard Site IDs -- valid but lost prior
-- to Dec-19", against the quality tier dashboard. Every TG site code
-- already matches a site_information row 1:1 (nothing is referentially
-- missing) -- the real signal is operational history, not existence.
-- Confirmed live: 976 sites never have first_pcn_sent_date populated (975
-- of those also never have live_date populated -- i.e. never actually went
-- live), and a further 406 sites issued PCNs but their LAST one predates
-- Dec 2019. Neither reproduces the client's exact 484/98 -- flagged as
-- Fabric's own best reconstruction of the same two concepts pending the
-- client's own query definition to reconcile exactly against (see the
-- 20260921 CCP Monthly Metrics extract for the full site-level list).
last_pcn_activity AS (
    SELECT
        site_id,
        MIN(issue_date) AS first_pcn_date,      -- go-live fallback for non-migrated sites
        MAX(issue_date) AS last_pcn_issue_date  -- lost-date fallback for non-migrated sites
    FROM {{ ref('core_pcn_legacy') }}
    GROUP BY site_id
),

-- FIX (2026-08-31, second pass): this CTE referenced cus.site_code/
-- cu.user_id/cu.max_cancellations, none of which exist on the live staged
-- tables -- client_user_sites/client_users have no metadata-seed rename
-- rows, so stage_clean's auto-snake-case leaves userid/sitecode/
-- maxcancellations unchanged (no case boundary to split on). Pre-existing
-- defect, unrelated to this pass's own changes -- surfaced because this is
-- the first time core_site_legacy has actually been rebuilt against the
-- current live schema since this CTE was written.
cancel_budget AS (
    SELECT
        {{ pcn_key('cus.site_code') }}   AS site_id,
        MAX(cu.max_cancellations)         AS monthly_free_cancel_budget
    FROM {{ ref('client_user_sites') }} cus
    JOIN {{ ref('client_users') }} cu ON cu.user_id = CAST(cus.user_id AS VARCHAR(20))  -- type mismatch: client_users.userid is varchar, client_user_sites.userid is int
    GROUP BY {{ pcn_key('cus.site_code') }}
)

SELECT
    b.site_sk,
    b.site_id,
    b.site_name,
    b.region,
    b.postcode AS postcode,
    b.disabled,
    b.disabled_letter,
    -- BUG FOUND LIVE 2026-09-16: site_nature and quality_tier are two
    -- genuinely different concepts (car-park type vs. quality ranking), but
    -- both were reading COALESCE(scl.site_nature, b.nature_of_site)
    -- unfiltered -- sitecategorytracking.category (scl.site_nature)
    -- actually holds a MIX of tier labels (Bronze/Silver/Gold, 2,550 of
    -- ~2,629 populated rows) and genuine car-park-type labels (Permit
    -- holders/Payment Car Park/Maximum stay/Manual/Customer member guest
    -- only/Other, ~79 rows), so site_nature was showing "Bronze" for the
    -- vast majority of sites instead of a car-park type. Confirmed live:
    -- Site Information.nature_of_site (the fallback) is a CLEAN
    -- car-park-type-only field with no tier values at all, so it was always
    -- the right fallback -- the fix is filtering the preferred source to
    -- its car-park-type values before falling back, not changing the
    -- fallback itself.
    COALESCE(
        CASE WHEN scl.site_nature NOT IN ('Bronze', 'Silver', 'Gold', 'Platinum', 'Low Performer')
             THEN scl.site_nature END,
        b.nature_of_site
    ) AS site_nature,
    b.business_category,
    srl.status_sub_reason,
    std.site_rule_type,
    std.popla_prefix,
    cal.customer_id,
    tl.tablet_type,
    COALESCE(stl.start_date, b.contract_start_date, CAST(lpa.first_pcn_date AS DATE))  AS contract_start_date,  -- site_terms -> Site Information -> PCN first-date fallback
    COALESCE(stl.end_date, b.contract_end_date)       AS contract_end_date,
    b.has_been_renewed,
    COALESCE(b.first_pcn_sent_date, CAST(lpa.first_pcn_date AS DATE)) AS first_pcn_sent_date,  -- PCN table fallback for non-migrated sites
    b.live_date,
    COALESCE(b.live_date, CAST(lpa.first_pcn_date AS DATE)) AS golive_date,  -- live_date preferred; PCN first-date fallback for non-migrated sites
    b.renewal_date,                                   -- best-candidate only, see header
    COALESCE(CAST(sdl.event_datetime AS DATE), CAST(lpa.last_pcn_issue_date AS DATE)) AS lost_date,  -- disable-event log preferred; PCN last-date fallback for non-migrated sites
    b.revenue_share_pct,
    CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(50))                         AS revenue_share_model,   -- no source, see header
    CAST(NULL AS INTEGER)                             AS spaces,                -- no source
    CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(20))                         AS size_band,             -- derived from spaces, which has no source
    CAST(NULL AS INTEGER)                             AS size_band_sort,
    CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR(20))                         AS pcn_rev_share_band,    -- derived from revenue_share_pct
    CAST(COALESCE(b.live_date, lpa.first_pcn_date) AS DATE) AS acquisition_date,  -- PCN first-date fallback for non-migrated sites
    CASE
        WHEN COALESCE(b.live_date, lpa.first_pcn_date) IS NULL
            THEN NULL
        WHEN MONTH(COALESCE(b.live_date, lpa.first_pcn_date)) >= 4
            THEN CONCAT('FY', RIGHT(CAST(YEAR(COALESCE(b.live_date, lpa.first_pcn_date)) + 1 AS VARCHAR(4)), 2))
        ELSE CONCAT('FY', RIGHT(CAST(YEAR(COALESCE(b.live_date, lpa.first_pcn_date)) AS VARCHAR(4)), 2))
    END                                                AS acquisition_fy,
    -- quality_tier: the tier-shaped subset of the SAME source column used
    -- for site_nature above, filtered the other way -- no separate tier
    -- source exists (see header), and NO fallback (nature_of_site never
    -- carries tier values either, confirmed live).
    CASE WHEN scl.site_nature IN ('Bronze', 'Silver', 'Gold', 'Platinum', 'Low Performer')
         THEN scl.site_nature END                          AS quality_tier,
    CASE scl.site_nature
        WHEN 'Bronze' THEN 1 WHEN 'Silver' THEN 2 WHEN 'Gold' THEN 3 WHEN 'Platinum' THEN 4 ELSE NULL
    END                                                AS quality_tier_rank,    -- 4-tier vocabulary, matches live core_site.sql -- see header
    CASE
        WHEN b.disabled = 1 THEN 'Disabled'
        WHEN b.disabled = 0 THEN 'Live - operational'
        ELSE NULL
    END                                                AS current_status,       -- matches the KPI's literal string, see header
    -- BUG FOUND LIVE 2026-09-17: TrafficGuard emits 'Live - operational'
    -- (lowercase 'o'), Zeus emits 'Live - Operational' (capital 'O') -- any
    -- exact-match filter on current_status across both systems silently
    -- drops whichever one it wasn't written for. current_status itself is
    -- left untouched (the KPI above depends on its exact casing, see
    -- header) -- this flag is a new, case-insensitive derivation any
    -- consumer can use instead of re-deriving the same UPPER() check.
    CAST(CASE WHEN b.disabled = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS BIT) AS is_live_operational_flag,
    CAST(b.contract_term AS DECIMAL(6,2))              AS contract_length_years,
    CAST(b.latest_contract_term AS DECIMAL(6,2))       AS latest_contract_length_years,  -- pairs with renewal_date, see header
    b.site_sales_channel,
    b.free_cancellation_limit,
    cb.monthly_free_cancel_budget,

    -- "non-existent": never actually went live / never issued a single PCN.
    -- Uses PCN table as fallback: sites with TG null but real PCN rows correctly show 0
    CAST(CASE WHEN COALESCE(b.first_pcn_sent_date, lpa.first_pcn_date) IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS BIT)
        AS never_operational_flag,

    -- "lost prior to Dec-19": issued PCNs at some point, but its last one
    -- predates December 2019 -- dormant, no longer under active management.
    lpa.last_pcn_issue_date,
    CAST(CASE
        WHEN b.first_pcn_sent_date IS NOT NULL
         AND lpa.last_pcn_issue_date IS NOT NULL
         AND lpa.last_pcn_issue_date < '2019-12-01'
        THEN 1 ELSE 0
    END AS BIT) AS dormant_pre_dec19_flag

FROM base b
LEFT JOIN site_type_decode std      ON std.site_type_id = b.site_type_id
LEFT JOIN site_category_latest scl  ON scl.site_id = b.site_id
LEFT JOIN site_reason_latest srl    ON srl.site_id = b.site_id
LEFT JOIN client_admin_latest cal   ON cal.site_id = b.site_id
LEFT JOIN site_terms_latest stl     ON stl.site_id = b.site_id
LEFT JOIN site_disabled_latest sdl  ON sdl.site_id = b.site_id
LEFT JOIN tablet_lookup tl          ON tl.site_id = b.site_id
LEFT JOIN cancel_budget cb          ON cb.site_id = b.site_id
LEFT JOIN last_pcn_activity lpa     ON lpa.site_id = b.site_id

model.ccp.core_site_lifecycle_legacy.name: core_site_lifecycle_legacy
model.ccp.core_site_lifecycle_legacy.raw_code:
{{ config(
    alias        = 'core_site_lifecycle_legacy',
    tags         = ['core', 'legacy', 'site_lifecycle']
) }}

-- =========================================================================
-- Entity: core_site_lifecycle_legacy
-- Grain : Up to 3 rows per legacy site (TrafficGuard):
--           - 'New'  : site acquisition / contract start
--           - 'Live' : site go-live (first operational day)
--           - 'Lost' : site churn / deactivation
--
-- Date resolution is handled upstream in core_site_legacy (COALESCE chain):
--   contract_start_date = site_terms.start_date  -> site_info.contract_date -> pcn.MIN(issue_date)
--   golive_date         = site_info.live_date     -> pcn.MIN(issue_date)
--   lost_date           = site_disabled_event     -> pcn.MAX(issue_date)
--
-- Migrated sites (also in Zeus) are excluded by fact_site_lifecycle's existing
-- NOT EXISTS filter on ccp_site.ccp_legacysitenumber. No change needed here.
-- =========================================================================

WITH period_ranked AS (

    SELECT
        site_id,
        start_date,
        end_date,
